items.title: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease: immune profiling and correlation of immune cells with pulmonary function in SSc-ILD.
items.abstract: Connective tissue diseases (CTDs) frequently involve the lungs, with CTD-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) representing a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet the immunopathological mechanisms remain incompletely defined. This study characterized immune profiles in CTD-ILD and their association with pulmonary function impairment, focusing on systemic sclerosis-associated ILD (SSc-ILD). This single-center retrospective study enrolled 217 CTD-ILD patients, 100 healthy controls, and 25 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Peripheral lymphocyte subsets, immunoglobulins, complements, and cytokines were assessed using flow cytometry and immunoturbidimetry. Lung function was evaluated by standard spirometry and gas transfer tests. Compared to healthy controls, lymphocyte counts were reduced in all ILD subtypes, lowest in polymyositis/dermatomyositis (PM/DM)-ILD. In SSc-ILD, T cell and helper T cell (Th) percentages were significantly elevated (76.2% and 49.39%, respectively). Complement C3 was lower in Sjögren's syndrome (SS)-ILD (889.92 vs. 965.49 mg/L), and C4 was significantly lower in SSc-ILD (196.74 vs. 226.70 mg/L) versus controls. SSc-ILD patients with higher Th cell proportions exhibited worse pulmonary function, with expiratory reserve volume (ERV) falling 57.21%, maximal vital capacity (VC max) 18.81%, functional residual capacity (FRC) 19.64%, forced vital capacity (FVC)17.93%, and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) 20.28%. Continuous correlation analysis further confirmed significant negative correlations between Th cell proportions and ERV, FRC, and PCO 2 . Peripheral blood immune profiling revealed distinct abnormalities across CTD-ILD subtypes. Peripheral Th cell expansion is strongly associated with lung function decline in SSc-ILD, highlighting the potential of Th cells as biomarkers of disease progression in SSc-ILD.

items.title: A Multi-Axis Plantar Load Measurement Platform for the Assessment of Foot Disorders: Comparison of Patients With Psoriatic Arthritis to a Healthy Control Cohort.
items.abstract: Accurate assessment of plantar loading, including shear forces, is crucial for understanding foot pathologies such as dactylitis in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Existing devices predominantly measure plantar pressures, neglecting important shear stresses which may initiate dactylitis. This study presents a novel multi-axis plantar load measurement platform to address this gap. The study utilised a newly developed plantar load measurement system, comprising a Hall-effect-based magnetic sensing array, custom data logging electronics, and tailored data processing software. The system's efficacy was evaluated in a pilot feasibility study involving patients with PsA with no, current, or previous dactylitis, and healthy controls. Participants walked barefoot on the platform, capturing plantar shear and pressure data. Shear stresses were notably higher in the second to fourth rays compared to other regions, particularly in the left foot, aligning with the hypothesis that repetitive local trauma might initiate dactylitis in PsA. However, no consistent differences in stresses were observed between diagnostic groups, likely due to small sample sizes and gait alterations associated with pain. A marked asymmetry was observed between the right and left feet, suggesting dominant-foot placement effects. The new platform demonstrates potential clinical utility in capturing comprehensive foot-loading profiles, including critical shear stresses previously under-assessed. Although the current pilot study was limited in number, the results support the theory that local mechanical stresses may contribute to PsA-related dactylitis. Future larger-scale studies are needed to clarify these findings and overcome limitations related to altered gait patterns due to foot pain.

items.title: Metabolic gatekeepers shape immune cell function in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Immune cell function is tightly coupled to cellular metabolism, with glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and amino acid and lipid metabolism governing activation, differentiation, survival, and effector responses. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), an autoimmune disease characterized by destructive joint inflammation, metabolic checkpoints have emerged as critical regulators of immune-cell behavior and drivers of tissue pathology. RA CD4+ T cells undergo profound metabolic reprogramming: glycolysis is suppressed, and glucose is redirected into the pentose phosphate pathway, resulting in NADPH accumulation, reduced ROS levels, and a highly reductive intracellular environment. Concurrent defects in mitochondrial DNA repair and electron transport chain function compromise mitochondrial fitness, leading to NAD+ depletion, altered tricarboxylic acid cycle activity, and metabolic exhaustion. The resulting accumulation of citrate and acetyl-CoA promotes lipogenesis and protein acetylation, driving membrane remodeling, tissue invasiveness, and proinflammatory effector functions. Depletion of oxaloacetate and aspartate limits NAD+ regeneration, inducing endoplasmic reticulum expansion and enhanced tumor necrosis factor production. Defective lysosomal coordination of AMPK and mTORC1 signaling uncouples energy sensing from anabolic programs, enabling cellular activation and proliferation despite metabolic insufficiency. Macrophage fate and function are similarly shaped by metabolic state. In synovial macrophages, GLUD1-dependent glutamine oxidation sustains mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, enabling survival under nutrient-deprived conditions while promoting antigen presentation. Conversely, metabolic stress in MerTK+ macrophages activates the NAD+ hydrolase SARM1, triggering NAD+ depletion, mitochondrial collapse, and PANoptotic cell death. Together, these findings identify NAD+ availability, mitochondrial fitness, and organelle-based signaling as central metabolic gatekeepers linking bioenergetic stress to immune-cell dysfunction and chronic inflammation in RA.

items.title: Identification of a systemic lupus erythematosus disease signature in resting naive B cells.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune condition with alternating phases of heightened symptoms and periods of disease inactivity. Our investigation focuses on the distinct molecular profiles of resting naive B cells from both active and inactive SLE states in female adults, primarily of Black ancestry. We identified a distinct transcriptome and epigenome during inactive SLE. Transcriptional patterns indicated an increase in distinct cytokine signaling pathway expression in SLE B cells, encompassing both common and disease activity-specific components. Specifically, while both disease states exhibited interferon signatures, increased expression of IL-12, TNF-α/NF-κB, and CD40 signaling pathway genes was enriched in inactive disease. While some regions exhibited comparable epigenetic features in both disease states, such as TLR7 signaling genes, others were distinct. Chromatin accessibility in inactive disease indicated the involvement of MEF2 and bHLH family factors, such as E2A/E2-2, while active disease regions were defined by IRF family factors. This study illuminates both disease-associated programs and molecular changes to cell activation pathways capable of directing B cells toward diverse effector fates in active or inactive SLE. Our data also offer insights of particular importance for the design and monitoring of B cell-targeting treatments.

items.title: Initial treatment strategies and outcomes across haemodynamic thresholds and risk stratification in incident systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: a EUSTAR analysis.
items.abstract: Real-world initial treatment strategies in SSc-PAH remain incompletely described. We aimed to characterise these strategies across haemodynamic thresholds and risk strata and evaluate outcome associations. We analysed treatment-naïve SSc-PAH patients in EUSTAR (2000-2021) fulfilling the 2022 haemodynamic definition. Initial therapy comprised treatment initiated within 4 months of RHC. As-treated (AT) analyses were primary and intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses supportive. Outcomes were all-cause mortality and 36-month PAH progression. Among 301 patients, 198 (66%) initiated therapy and 170 maintained therapy for ≥3 months. Therapy was initiated in 31% with milder haemodynamic impairment (mPAP 21-24 mmHg and/or PVR 2-3 WU) versus 79% fulfilling the previous haemodynamic definition; combination therapy increased from 14% to 67% across low- to high-risk strata. Over a median 3.9 years, 125 (42%) died and 85/227 (37%) progressed. Adjusted ITT analyses showed no association with either outcome, whereas adjusted AT analyses showed lower mortality risk with sustained monotherapy and combination therapy (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.27-0.92 and HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.88, respectively) and lower PAH progression risk with sustained initial therapy (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.18-0.76). In the milder haemodynamic subgroup, the mortality estimate was directionally consistent but imprecise. Initial treatment strategies reflected haemodynamic severity and baseline risk, while variation suggested potential implementation gaps. Sustained initial therapy was associated with lower risks of mortality and PAH progression. Contrasting ITT and AT estimates highlight challenges in observational treatment-outcome comparisons. Findings in the milder haemodynamic subgroup support dedicated prospective studies.

items.title: Central sensitization in rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional analysis of functional disability, disease activity, and glucocorticoid use.
items.abstract: To examine the clinical correlates of central sensitization (CS) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to perform an exploratory analysis of its association with glucocorticoid use. This single-center, cross-sectional study included 286 patients with RA (≥18 years) fulfilling the 2010 EULAR/ACR classification criteria and receiving stable treatment for at least 3 months. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and treatment history were recorded. Participants completed the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) and the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with CS. CS was present in 31.5% ( n  = 90) of patients. Patients with CS exhibited significantly higher tender joint counts and DAS28-CRP scores, while CRP levels and swollen joint counts were comparable between groups. In univariable analyses, CS was associated with younger age, female sex, longer disease duration, greater biologic exposure, and more frequent current steroid use (54.4% vs. 34.7%, p  = 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression revealed that higher HAQ scores remained the sole independent factor associated with CS (OR: 5.32, p  < 0.001), whereas the initial association with corticosteroid use lost significance after adjustment. CS in RA is independently linked to functional disability rather than objective inflammation, highlighting a potential discordance between clinical findings and symptom burden. Recognition of these non-inflammatory mechanisms may help prevent unnecessary treatment escalation, particularly glucocorticoid overuse, and support more appropriate pain management strategies.

items.title: Metabolic-Epigenetic Reprogramming of Fibroblast-Like Synoviocytes in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Perspectives for Traditional Chinese Medicine.
items.abstract: In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), persistent synovial inflammation and clinical relapse cannot be fully explained by immune activation alone, as fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) can acquire stable pathogenic states that sustain synovitis and joint destruction. Metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodeling are functionally integrated in RA-FLS, thereby promoting hyperproliferation, invasiveness, apoptosis resistance, and inflammatory memory. In this review, we summarize the interplay between altered cellular metabolism and epigeneticmechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, RNA modifications, and chromatin remodeling, and discuss how this interplay contributes tostabilizing pathogenic FLS phenotypes.We further discuss gut microbiota-associated metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, tryptophan derivatives, and one-carbon metabolites, as potential mediators linking systemic metabolic imbalance to FLS epigenetic states. These metabolites may act through histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition, modulation of methyl donor availability, and receptor-mediated inflammatory signaling. From the perspective of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), we propose that TCM formulations and bioactive compounds may modulate this network through microbiota-dependent metabolic remodeling and direct suppression of FLS activation. Finally, we identify current evidence gaps and highlight emerging therapeutic strategies, including metabolomics-guided fecal microbiota transplantation and FLS-targeted epigenetic interventions. This review highlights metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming as a key mechanism underlying persistent RA-FLS phenotypes. Interactions among thegut microbiota, microbial metabolites, and epigenetic regulation provide a promising framework for linking systemic metabolic disturbances to local joint damage. Future studies integrating multi-omics profiling, microbiome modulation, and FLS-targeted epigenetic interventions are needed to clarify causality and facilitate more precise therapeutic strategies.

items.title: African recommendations for diagnosis and management of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) - a PAFLAR initiative.
items.abstract: To develop evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of children and adolescents with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA), taking into consideration the socioeconomic status and availability of medications in African countries. A steering group composed of five PAFLAR members formulated questions in PICO format (Patient/Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome), conducted a systematic literature review, and identified experts in pediatric rheumatology throughout Africa. The Delphi method was used to reach consensus among the experts on the recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of sJIA patients. The online Delphi questionnaire was sent to the 22 experts selected by the steering committee, who were asked to vote for each statement and to provide their suggestions for modifications or rewording. A 100% response rate was obtained. A minimum agreement of 70% among the voting panel was required. A total of 15 recommendations were formulated, 4 regarding diagnosis and 11 regarding treatment. The percentage of agreement with the recommendations ranged from 72.7% to 95%. We present the first African recommendations for diagnosis and management of sJIA. The feedback about the application of these recommendations in pediatric rheumatology centers will serve as the basis for future revisions in the light of African-specific experiences and insights.

items.title: Cutaneous efficacy and glucocorticoid-sparing effects of anifrolumab in systemic lupus erythematosus: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: To evaluate the cutaneous efficacy and glucocorticoid-sparing effects of anifrolumab in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and to assess composite disease activity and flare-related and safety outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 20 April 2026. Meta-analyses were restricted to randomized controlled trials comparing intravenous anifrolumab 300 mg every 4 weeks plus standard therapy with placebo plus standard therapy; TULIP-SC and overlapping reports were synthesized narratively. Risk ratios (RRs) or rate ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models in the primary analyses, with fixed-effect models applied in sensitivity analyses. Modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) sensitivity analyses were performed for outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and a small number of contributing studies. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2 and GRADE, respectively. In all, 12 reports from five independent trials were included; four intravenous trials contributed up to 1,203 participants. The Week 52 CLASI-A50 estimate was based on two trials (n = 165), not the full 1,203-participant IV evidence set. Random-effects pooling showed that anifrolumab improved Week 52 CLASI-A50 response based on two trials among patients with baseline CLASI-A ≥ 10 (RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.04 to 2.24), sustained oral glucocorticoid reduction in those receiving ≥ 10 mg/day at baseline (RR 1.56, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.87), and BICLA response (RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.41 to 1.94). SRI-4 (RR 1.39, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.87; I² = 80.8%), LLDAS attainment (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.73; I² = 57.2%), and annualized flare rate (rate ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.91; I² = 56.5%) favored anifrolumab but were affected by heterogeneity or limited trial numbers. The incidence of any adverse events was slightly higher (RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.16), whereas serious adverse events and discontinuations due to adverse events did not differ significantly. Supplementary analyses of selected adverse events of clinical interest suggested an increased risk of herpes zoster (RR 3.88, 95% CI 1.70 to 8.89), although event numbers were limited and these analyses were supplementary. Modified HKSJ sensitivity analyses yielded wider intervals crossing the null for SRI-4, LLDAS, annualized flare rate, serious adverse events, and adverse events leading to discontinuation. Intravenous anifrolumab improved Week 52 CLASI-A50 response in the two contributing trials of patients with baseline CLASI-A ≥ 10 and facilitated sustained glucocorticoid reduction in the prespecified glucocorticoid subgroup. DerSimonian-Laird point estimates for secondary efficacy outcomes generally favored anifrolumab, but the HKSJ sensitivity analyses for heterogeneous outcomes and the limited safety data warrant cautious interpretation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261367219.

items.title: Dynamic changes in CBC-derived inflammatory indices before and during acute coronary syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a within-patient paired study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with excess cardiovascular risk, but within-patient changes in complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices at the onset of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are not well described. We compared pre-event and acute-phase values in the same patients and contextualized pre-event values against a healthy cohort. This retrospective, single-center, within-patient paired study reviewed hospital records from July 1, 2018, to December 30, 2025 (approximately 90 months). Among 3,960 hospitalized patients with RA, 89 had clinician-confirmed ACS and qualifying paired CBC measurements. Acute-phase CBCs were obtained within 24 hours after symptom onset, and pre-event CBCs were the most recent routine measurements obtained more than 14 days before the event. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated and natural log-transformed. Pre-event values were also compared with a healthy cohort (n = 110), with age- and sex-adjusted analyses used because residual demographic imbalance was present. Pre-event log(NLR), log(SII), and log(SIRI) were higher in the RA cohort than in healthy controls and remained higher after adjustment for age and sex (all P< 0.001). Within-patient analyses showed increases during ACS, with mean Δlog values of 0.466 for NLR, 0.508 for SII, and 0.381 for SIRI (all Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q< 0.001). Neutrophilia increased from 11.2% before the event to 41.6% during ACS (McNemar P< 0.001). Exploratory subgroup estimates were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across several small strata; changes did not differ materially between remission/low and moderate/high RA activity groups. Among patients with RA who developed ACS, CBC-derived inflammatory indices were higher than in a healthy comparison cohort before the event and increased further within the first 24 hours of ACS. The paired design quantifies change relative to each patient's own pre-event value. Without a non-RA ACS comparator, however, the study cannot establish RA-specific inflammatory priming or a causal chronic-to-acute mechanism. Prospective studies with serial sampling and clinical outcomes are needed.

items.title: Case Report: Value of MR relaxometry and spectroscopy in multimodal imaging characterization of limbic encephalitis in systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Central nervous system involvement is uncommon in systemic sclerosis, and inflammatory temporomesial syndromes in this context are rarely reported. We present a 58-year-old man with systemic sclerosis who developed subacute cognitive impairment and dialeptic seizures arising from the right temporal lobe. Video electroencephalography confirmed a right temporal seizure onset zone. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated enlargement and subtle T2 hyperintensity of the right hippocampus and amygdala, while fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography images showed focal hypermetabolism of the enlarged right amygdala. Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated bilateral reduction of total N-acetylaspartate compared with an age-matched healthy reference subject, with a more pronounced difference on the right, a pattern compatible with bilateral, right-accentuated neuronal dysfunction or injury. MR relaxometry demonstrated significant bilateral T2 prolongation in the amygdalae and hippocampal heads, whereas T1 abnormalities were more region-dependent, involving the right amygdala and both hippocampal heads. Serum testing detected anti-pyruvate dehydrogenase antibodies, whereas routine clinical neural antibody testing was negative. The patient became seizure-free under antiseizure medication and immunosuppressive therapy with cyclophosphamide. Notably, although the unilateral conventional imaging findings did not meet the bilateral mesial temporal criterion required by current consensus criteria for definite autoimmune limbic encephalitis, MR relaxometry revealed bilateral temporomesial abnormalities. This finding is consistent with available neuropathological and experimental evidence and suggests that routine imaging may underestimate disease extent. This case highlights a rare presentation of antibody-atypical limbic encephalitis in the setting of systemic sclerosis and illustrates how multimodal imaging can support diagnosis and tissue characterization when routine antibody testing is unrevealing.

items.title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
items.abstract: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation. Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; p  = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year. JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

items.title: Radiomics-Based prediction of renal prognosis in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: To develop and validate a non-invasive prediction model combining renal CT radiomics features and clinical markers for assessing long-term renal prognosis at 1, 3, and 5 years in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV). A retrospective cohort of 262 AAV patients from Peking Union Medical College Hospital (2015-2020) was analyzed. Radiomics features (morphological, first-order, and texture) were extracted from segmented renal parenchyma on abdominopelvic CT. Clinical markers included demographics, serum creatinine, complement component 3 (C3), and other laboratory indicators. Renal volume, serum creatinine, and complement component 3 (C3) were pre-specified as predictors based on a priori biological rationale, and XGBoost was employed for model construction. Performance was evaluated via ROC-AUC (receiver operating characteristic/area under the curve), F1 score, decision curve analysis, and calibration curves. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis assessed feature contributions, and Kaplan-Meier curves with Bonferroni-corrected log-rank tests were used for survival stratification. The mean follow-up was 40.8 months; 59 patients (23%) developed ESRD (56 within 3 years) and 29 (11%) died. The combined model (renal volume + sCr + C3) achieved an AUC of 0.93 for 3-year ESRD prediction (clinical-only model: 0.91), with renal volume independently associated with ESRD (Wald p  = 0.004). For the 3-year composite outcome, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.84 (clinical-only: 0.81) with significantly improved reclassification (IDI p  = 0.018; category-free NRI p  = 0.024). In pre-specified median-based Kaplan-Meier analyses, reduced renal volume (≤ 130.6 mL), elevated serum creatinine (> 177.5 μmol/L) and lower C3 (≤ 0.97 g/L) were associated with poorer 3-year ESRD-free survival (log-rank p  ≤ 0.002). The integrated radiomics-clinical model provides accurate, non-invasive risk stratification for long-term renal outcomes in AAV, facilitating personalized treatment.

items.title: Malignant erythema as a high-specificity cutaneous indicator of malignancy in adult dermatomyositis: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is associated with a substantially elevated risk of malignancy, yet the cutaneous features predictive of cancer risk in adults remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to characterize cutaneous manifestations and clinical factors associated with malignancy in adult DM, with a focus on malignant erythema. This retrospective cohort study included 261 adults with DM admitted between 2016 and 2023 and followed up till June 2025. Clinical data, laboratory indicators (including creatine kinase [CK] and lactate dehydrogenase [LDH]), autoantibodies, and skin findings were systematically evaluated. The primary outcome was the occurrence of malignant tumors. Twenty‑six patients (10%) developed malignancy. Malignant erythema was identified in 35 patients (13.3%), among whom 14 (40%) had malignancy. Both anti-transcription intermediary factor-1 γ (anti-TIF-1 γ) antibodies and malignant erythema were independently associated with malignancy (odds ratio [OR] = 18.231, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.568-72.756, P < 0.001; OR = 17.588, 95% CI 2.151-143.824, P = 0.007). Malignant erythema demonstrated higher specificity for tumor prediction than anti-TIF-1 γ antibodies (91.1% vs. 86%, P < 0.001), while sensitivity did not differ significantly (53.8% vs. 73.1%, P = 0.190). while. Malignant erythema is a distinctive poikilodermatous manifestation strongly associated with malignancy in adult DM. Its high specificity suggests that malignant erythema may serve as a valuable clinical indicator for malignancy risk and a useful complement to anti-TIF-1 γ antibody testing.

items.title: Complement-amplified thrombotic microangiopathy in systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: a systematic review of 78 reported patients.
items.abstract: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) complicating systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis (LN) spans immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, anti-phospholipid-associated microangiopathy, secondary endothelial injury, and complement-amplified/atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS)-like phenotypes. The boundaries remain uncertain, and treatment evidence is dominated by selectively published cases. In this PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420261409684), we searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through to 17 March 2026, verified the source identity and eligibility, and performed a PubMed-only update through to 14 August 2026. We reconstructed patient-level reports by phenotype, competing mechanisms, complement-related evidence, treatment, and outcome. We included citable published abstracts when patient-level data were extractable but analyzed them as a lower-information stratum rather than as equivalent to full texts. Analyses were descriptive. We did not include China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) because no verifiable search record was available. One reviewer performed the screening, extraction, and appraisal. We report both as protocol deviations. We included 56 sources describing 78 patients: in total, 39 full-text sources/61 patients and 17 published abstract sources/17 patients. There were 56 female patients (71.8%), and the median age was 24.5 years. Source-adjudicated microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury/renal failure, strict TMA identified on kidney biopsy, and dialysis/renal replacement therapy (RRT) were present in 71 (91.0%), 74 (94.9%), 67 (85.9%), 42 (53.8%), and 46 (59.0%), respectively. Low C3/C4 levels were reported in 55 (70.5%), strict T2 complement evidence in 1 (1.3%), and index event terminal/tissue activation in 6 (7.7%). Complement inhibitors were reported in 60 (76.9%) and renal and hematologic improvements in 49 (62.8%) and 65 (83.3%), respectively. Certainty was very low, and treatment comparisons were not estimable. SLE/LN-associated TMA is heterogeneous, and complement may act as a driver, an amplifier, or an epiphenomenon. Case-based evidence supports rigorous mechanistic adjudication and biomarker-rich registries, but cannot establish incidence, prognosis, comparative efficacy, or universal treatment duration. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261409684, identifier CRD420261409684.

items.title: IL-23 and monocyte interactions redirect human Th17.1 cells to an IL-17A high IFN-γ high potentially pathogenic profile.
items.abstract: IL-23-targeted therapies have demonstrated clinical efficacy in psoriatic arthritis (PsA), primarily through the reduction of IL-17A-driven inflammation. Consequently, most studies have focused on classical, high IL-17A-producing, CCR6 + CXCR3 - CCR4 + Th17 cells. In contrast, the impact of IL‑23 signaling on CCR6 + CXCR3 + CCR4 - Th17.1 cells -traditionally characterized by high IFN-γ and low IL-17A production-remains largely unexplored, despite their recognized pathogenicity in autoimmune disease. The aim of this study was to characterize the effects of IL-23 on human memory Th17.1 cells. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from treatment-naive patients with early PsA were stimulated in the presence of IL-23 or anti-IL-23 antibody before quantifying IL-17A and IFN-γ secretion. Additionally, human memory CCR6 - Th1, CCR6 + Th17.1 and CCR6+ Th17 cells from healthy donors were sorted and analyzed ex vivo for IL23R , TBX21 and RORC expression using RT-qPCR. Sorted Th17.1, Th17 and Th1 cells were subsequently cultured alone or cocultured with IL-23-producing monocytes. Cultures received either exogenous IL-23 or IL-23 inhibition before analyzing IL-17A and IFN-γ secretion. As expected, IL-23 stimulation induced IL-17A in PsA PBMCs, whereas IL-23 inhibition reduced IL-17A secretion but did not affect IFN-γ. In healthy donor PBMCs, ex vivo IL-23R expression was restricted to memory CCR6 + Th17 and Th17.1 cells. Remarkably, IL-23 stimulation of Th17.1 cells significantly increased IFN-γ without affecting IL-17A secretion. Compared to monoculture, cocultures with monocytes increased IFN-γ secretion in Th17.1 and classical Th1 cells, and IL-17A secretion in Th17 and Th17.1 cells. Additional IL-23 stimulated IL-17A in both Th17 and Th17.1 cocultures, while unexpectedly reducing IFN-γ in Th17.1 cells. In contrast, IL-23 inhibition reduced IL-17A secretion in Th17 and Th17.1 cells without affecting IFN-γ production. IL-23 exerts distinct effects on Th17.1 compared to Th17 cells. We show a role for IL-23 in IFN-γ upregulation in Th17.1 cells, which is reversed in the presence of monocytes. In co-culture with monocytes, Th17.1 cells progress to a pathogenic IL-17A high IFN-γ high profile, which is further elevated by IL-23 stimulation and reduced upon IL-23 neutralization. We show that IL-23 drives Th17.1 plasticity and underscore the therapeutic relevance of neutralizing IL-23 in the suppression of these pathogenic IL-17A high IFN-γ high Th17.1 cells.

items.title: Case Report: Relapse of SLE associated with EBV infection in a patient after CAR-T cell therapy: a clinical case.
items.abstract: We present the case of a 13-year-old boy with refractory systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) who achieved drug-free remission after anti-CD19 CAR-T cell therapy, but subsequently experienced Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) reactivation on day 142 after CAR T-cell infusion and peak EBV load was 24,400 IU/mL with a severe drop in platelets to 8×10 9 /L, which leading to relapse of SLE and manifestations of chronic active EBV disease (CAEBVD). The whole exogenous gene testing found X chromosome Xp22.33q28 region (chrX: 200855-155239820) a duplicate of about 155.04Mbp,which is associated with the development of Klinefelter syndrome (KS).The temporal association between EBV resurgence and SLE flare suggests that CAR-T-induced immunosuppression with some genetic background may permit EBV reactivation, which can be associated with the return of autoimmunity. This case highlights the need for vigilant monitoring for opportunistic infections and genetic background, particularly EBV, after CAR-T therapy for autoimmune diseases, as they may contribute to disease relapse.

items.title: Clinical case series: Emergence of psoriatic arthritis during biologic IL-23 pathway inhibition therapy for psoriasis.
items.abstract: Psoriasis (PsO) and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) are increasingly recognized as manifestations within the spectrum of psoriatic disease, and emerging observational data suggest that biologic therapy targeting interleukin-23 (IL-23) may reduce the risk of incident PsA. This finding remains controversial given the potential for channeling and information bias. Here, we describe five patients with long-standing PsO who developed new-onset PsA while achieving excellent skin clearance with IL-23 or IL-12/23 inhibitor therapy (risankizumab in four patients and ustekinumab in one). The time from the initiation of IL-23 pathway inhibition to PsA diagnosis ranged from 5 to 63 months. All patients met the ClASsification criteria for Psoriatic ARthritis, with musculoskeletal manifestations including dactylitis, synovitis, tenosynovitis, and enthesitis, and two patients had erosive changes on imaging. Joint symptoms improved in the majority of patients after transition to an IL-17-targeted biologic. These cases indicate that IL-23 pathway inhibition may not reliably prevent the onset of PsA and may contribute to its development in susceptible individuals. Thus, this series underscores the importance of ongoing musculoskeletal surveillance in patients with PsO receiving IL-23-targeted therapy, even when skin disease is completely controlled.

items.title: T cells form distinct spatially restricted immune responses in synovium of patients with psoriasis arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are chronic, inflammatory joint diseases, causing progressive structural damage. Non-immune cells, such as stromal fibroblasts promote inflammation, cartilage degradation and bone resorption in the synovium. Here, we hypothesized that lining fibroblasts have distinct immune cell neighborhoods in PsA and RA. The spatial distribution of structural and immune cell populations was determined using high-multiplex immunohistochemistry in synovial biopsies from 9 PsA and 6 RA patients without previous methotrexate (MTX) treatment and 11 PsA and 11 RA patients treated with MTX treatment. Dendritic cells and macrophages exhibited strong patient-specific variability, whereas the numbers and localization of T cell subpopulations displayed patterns specific to the disease and treatment. Quantification of overall cell numbers in the synovium revealed a higher Th1/Th2 ratio in PsA than in RA. MTX-treated PsA, patients showed lower Th1 and higher Th2 numbers, whereas in RA, Th1, Th2 and Th9 numbers were less abundant. Spatial analysis revealed two regions with distinct immune responses around the lining fibroblasts. In PsA, the immediate vicinity of the lining fibroblasts was dominated by Th1/Th17 cells, followed by a region with a predominant Th2/Th9 cell population. In RA, a barrier-focused immune response consisting of Th9, Th17, and Th22 cells was observed near the lining fibroblasts. MTX-treated patients had lower the number of Th cells near the lining fibroblasts in PsA but did not differ in Th subtype patterns. In RA, lower Th numbers were mainly observed in the immediate vicinity of the lining fibroblasts, with distinct alterations in the numbers of Th22 and Th2 cells. In PsA, the immediate vicinity of lining fibroblasts is dominated by Th1/Th17/DC2 cells. In RA, a Th9/Th17/Th22 barrier-centered immune response was present near the lining; Th1 and Th2 cells were essentially absent. Patients treated with MTX had 50% fewer Th cells in this area in both PsA and RA, but increased Th1 numbers in RA. These findings may help explain the different therapeutic responses in these diseases.

items.title: Mycophenolate mofetil as salvage therapy for refractory acute-onset CIDP associated with rheumatoid arthritis: a case report.
items.abstract: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) is an immune-mediated neuropathy that rarely co-occurs with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). When CIDP proves refractory to first-line therapies, management becomes particularly challenging, especially in patients with multiple autoimmune conditions. A 43-year-old Chinese male with a 3-year history of seropositive RA in sustained remission presented with acute progressive quadriparesis, bilateral ptosis, and facial diplegia. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed albuminocytologic dissociation, and nerve conduction studies demonstrated evolving demyelinating features, consistent with a diagnosis of acute-onset CIDP (A-CIDP). The patient responded inadequately to sequential treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, high-dose corticosteroids, and the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) antagonist efgartigimod, experiencing repeated relapses during corticosteroid tapering. Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) was subsequently introduced as a steroid-sparing agent at 0.75 g twice daily, enabling further prednisone tapering from 20 mg to 10 mg daily without relapse; MMF was later up-titrated to 1 g twice daily. Under a combined, multi-target immunosuppressive regimen of MMF, prednisone, methotrexate, iguratimod, and hydroxychloroquine, the patient achieved sustained neurological improvement, with prednisone successfully tapered to 10 mg daily by October 2025 and maintained thereafter. By April 2026, only residual mild ptosis persisted, and no infectious complications occurred. This case suggests that MMF-based multi-target immunosuppression may be a therapeutic option for RA-associated, treatment-refractory A-CIDP, potentially enabling successful glucocorticoid tapering even after an inadequate response to a short course of FcRn-targeted therapy.

items.title: False-Positive HIV Screening in New-Onset Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Presenting with Polyserositis and Lupus Nephritis.
items.abstract: False-reactive human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) screening can occur in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and may delay recognition of the underlying autoimmune disease. A 23-year-old woman presented with weight loss, polyserositis and nephrotic-range proteinuria. Her HIV antigen/antibody screen was reactive, but supplemental testing did not confirm HIV infection. Lupus serologies, hypocomplementemia and kidney biopsy established SLE with mixed proliferative and membranous lupus nephritis. Recurrent pleural and progressive pericardial effusions required immunosuppression, pericardial drainage, a surgical window and pleural decortication. The reactive HIV screen initially favoured an infectious diagnosis; however, proteinuria, haematuria and low complement levels suggested immune-complex disease. This illustrates the risk of diagnostic anchoring on a preliminary screening result. A reactive HIV screen is not diagnostic. Prompt supplemental testing and parallel evaluation for autoimmune disease can prevent delayed diagnosis of SLE. A reactive HIV screening assay is preliminary, not diagnostic; in patients with autoimmune features, prompt supplemental testing is essential because systemic lupus erythematosus can cause false reactivity.A reactive HIV screen may create diagnostic anchoring when weight loss, serosal effusions and renal abnormalities coexist; discordant clinical and laboratory findings should trigger reassessment rather than premature attribution to HIV.In a young patient with unexplained polyserositis, proteinuria and glomerular haematuria, early lupus serology, complement testing and careful family history can expedite the diagnosis of severe lupus nephritis.

items.title: Behçet's Disease in Non-Endemic Areas: A Delayed Diagnosis in A Young Male With Recurrent Bipolar Aphthosis.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease (BD) is a rare chronic multisystem inflammatory disorder characterized by vasculitis of vessels of any caliber. It is classically associated with populations along the ancient Silk Road (from the Mediterranean basin to the Far East), but increasing numbers of cases are now reported in non-endemic regions, where delayed diagnosis is common due to low clinical suspicion and the absence of specific diagnostic biomarkers. We report the case of a 28-year-old man from Mexico with an 18-month history of recurrent painful oral ulcers, later associated with genital ulcers, arthralgias, and cutaneous lesions. The patient had been previously evaluated by multiple physicians and received several empirical treatments without improvement. Physical examination revealed multiple oral and genital ulcers, erythematous macular lesions on the palms and soles, and acneiform lesions on the back. Laboratory and immunological studies were unremarkable, and ophthalmological evaluation was normal. After exclusion of infectious and autoimmune diseases, Behçet's disease was suspected. The patient met the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease (ICBD, 2014) with a total of 5 points. Treatment with azathioprine and prednisone led to progressive clinical improvement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of Behçet's disease in non-endemic regions. Awareness of its heterogeneous clinical spectrum and the use of validated clinical criteria are essential to avoid diagnostic delay and prevent irreversible organ damage. Behçet's disease should be suspected in patients with recurrent bipolar aphthosis, even in non-endemic regions.The absence of specific biomarkers and histological findings contributes significantly to delayed diagnosis.The International Criteria for Behçet's Disease (ICBD, 2014) provide a sensitive and practical clinical tool for recognizing incomplete but clinically relevant forms of the disease.

items.title: Diagnosis and management of giant cell arteritis.
items.abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is the most common form of vasculitis affecting patients above the age of 50. Over the past few decades, our understanding of the pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and treatment of the disease has increased tremendously. We now recognize that there is more than just the compromise of the temporal artery and its branches. Advances in technology and immunology have led to new diagnostic imaging methods and more targeted treatments with fewer side effects. The aim of this review is to summarize the advances in the presentation, diagnosis, and treatment of GCA.

items.title: Persistent HyperCKemia Beyond Post-Viral Myositis: A Case of Anti-HMGCR Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy.
items.abstract: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy that should be suspected in patients with progressive proximal muscle weakness and marked creatine kinase (CK) elevation persisting despite statin discontinuation, although distinguishing it from more common conditions such as post-viral myositis and toxic statin-associated myopathy remains a major diagnostic challenge. We report the case of a 64-year-old man receiving long-term atorvastatin therapy who presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, and severe hyperCKemia following a self-limited flu-like illness, initially raising post-viral myositis as the leading hypothesis. Despite immediate statin discontinuation and aggressive intravenous hydration, severe hyperCKemia persisted during the first week of supportive management alone, and the neurological deficits did not improve, prompting further investigation and empirical immunosuppression. Muscle magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multifocal inflammatory muscle edema, while extensive investigation for infectious, metabolic, endocrine, neoplastic, and autoimmune causes was unrevealing. Muscle biopsy showed a necrotizing myopathy with pauci-inflammatory features, and anti-HMGCR antibodies, which had not been included in the initial extended myositis panel and required a dedicated request, were subsequently identified, confirming statin-associated IMNM. Treatment with high-dose corticosteroids followed by methotrexate produced progressive biochemical improvement and complete recovery of muscle strength and swallowing function, with CK falling to 376 U/L (N 30-200 U/L) at the last follow-up (four months after admission). The principal educational value of this case lies in the diagnostic reasoning rather than in the diagnosis itself: it was the failure of the clinical and biochemical course to follow the anticipated trajectory, rather than the initial presentation, that prompted reconsideration of the working hypothesis. Dysphagia, less commonly reported in post-viral myositis and toxic statin-associated myopathy, together with persistent severe hyperCKemia despite statin withdrawal, should prompt evaluation for anti-HMGCR IMNM.

items.title: Clinical, Functional, and Radiological Profile of Patients With Spondyloarthritis: A Cross-Sectional Study From a Tertiary Care Center in Central India.
items.abstract: Spondyloarthritis (SpA) includes a group of chronic inflammatory rheumatic disorders, such as ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, enteropathic arthritis, and undifferentiated SpA, unified by shared genetic, clinical, and immunopathological features. Comprehensive clinical profiling of SpA patients, including disease activity, functional status, and structural complications such as vertebral fracture, remains limited in Indian tertiary care settings. This study aims to describe the sociodemographic, clinical, radiological, and biochemical profile of patients with SpA, including disease activity and functional status using validated indices (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI), Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score with C-reactive protein (ASDAS-CRP), and Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI)), and to assess associations between these measures, inflammatory markers, and the presence of vertebral fractures, a structural complication anticipated to be uncommon in this cohort. This hospital-based, cross-sectional, observational study was conducted in the Department of General Medicine of a tertiary care teaching hospital. Fifty adult patients diagnosed with SpA per the European Spondyloarthropathy Study Group (ESSG) criteria were enrolled by consecutive sampling. We performed detailed clinical evaluation, radiological assessment (modified New York criteria for sacroiliitis and vertebral fracture), and laboratory investigations (including HLA-B27 typing). Disease activity and function were assessed using BASDAI, ASDAS-CRP, and BASFI. Data were analyzed using SPSS Statistics version 26.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA); categorical variables were compared using the chi-square/Fisher's exact test and continuous variables using the Student's t-test/Mann-Whitney U test, with p<0.05 considered statistically significant. Given the anticipated small number of vertebral fracture events, all fracture-related comparisons were pre-specified as exploratory. The cohort had a mean age of 41.8 ± 10.9 years with a male predominance (74%). Ankylosing spondylitis was the most common subtype (54%), and axial involvement was present in 56% of patients; HLA-B27 was positive in 80%. Musculoskeletal (enthesitis, dactylitis) and extra-articular manifestations were noted in 64% of patients overall, most commonly enthesitis (38%) and uveitis (16%). Radiologically, 54% had grade III-IV sacroiliitis, and 12% (n=6) had vertebral fractures (predominantly thoracic, 50%). Fracture prevalence was numerically higher with longer disease duration (p=0.018) and higher erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)/C-reactiive protein (CRP) (p=0.038 and p=0.021, respectively). High disease activity was observed in 72% of patients (BASDAI ≥4.0) and 74% (ASDAS-CRP >2.1); 68% had moderate-to-severe functional limitation (BASFI ≥4.0). Spondyloarthritis in this cohort predominantly affected young to middle-aged men from rural and lower socioeconomic backgrounds, with a high burden of active disease and structural damage. Vertebral fractures were more frequent with longer disease duration and higher inflammatory markers in this exploratory analysis. The need for early diagnosis, routine disease-activity monitoring, and clinical vigilance for vertebral fracture as an under-recognized structural complication is imperative in resource-limited settings.

items.title: Circulating anti-Ro/Sjögren's syndrome-related antigen A antibodies and risk of heart rate-corrected QT interval prolongation: a meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that anti-Ro/Sjögren's syndrome-related antigen A (SSA) antibodies, specifically the anti-Ro/SSA-52kD subtype, can promote heart rate-corrected QT interval (QTc) prolongation by inhibiting the hERG-K + channel. However, the numerous clinical studies published over the past two decades yielded conflicting results. This meta-analysis aims at pooling the available data to provide clarity on this clinically relevant issue. A systematic review was performed for clinical studies comparing QTc in anti-Ro/SSA-positive vs. -negative subjects. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and odds ratios (ORs) were compared using random effects models. The risk of bias was assessed using RoBANS2, Egger's test and contour-enhanced funnel plots. Twenty-five studies were included, pooling 2122 anti-Ro/SSA-positive and 8865 anti-Ro/SSA-negative subjects. Overall, anti-Ro/SSA-positivity is associated with a longer QTc [SMD = 0.36 (0.18-0.53), P < 0.001], and a more than two times higher risk of QTc prolongation [OR = 2.24 (1.54-3.27), P < 0.001]. Several sub-analyses supported and refined these findings. Specifically, in anti-Ro/SSA-positive patients with unselected connective tissue disease, QTc absolute values are higher [SMD = 0.56 (0.20-0.93), P = 0.0026] and QTc prolongation occurs more frequently [OR = 6.99 (2.35-20.75), P < 0.001] than in negative patients; furthermore, QTc prolongation is also more common in systemic lupus erythematosus patients with circulating anti-Ro/SSA-antibodies than in those without [OR = 1.86 (1.19-2.90), P = 0.006]. Finally, in anti-Ro/SSA-52kD-positive subjects, the QTc is longer compared to the negative ones [SMD = 0.43 (0.15-0.71), P = 0.002]. This meta-analysis supports the conclusion that circulating anti-Ro/SSA-antibodies per se represents a significant risk factor for QTc prolongation. However, the presence of several conflicting studies suggests that a more accurate investigation of specific factors, such as the impact of individual antibody subtype levels (anti-52kD/anti-60kD), will be critical to fully clarify the topic and its implications in clinical practice.

items.title: Case report: Incidental finding of a duplicated right vertebral artery in a 17-year-old female with suspected systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: We present the case of a 17-year-old female with suspected systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), receiving prednisolone and hydroxychloroquine, who was evaluated for a difference in blood pressure between the upper extremities and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). CT angiography (CTA) of the cervical vessels, performed because of clinical suspicion of vasculitis, incidentally demonstrated duplication of the right vertebral artery (VA), with both limbs originating from the right subclavian artery. The medial limb coursed posterior to the common carotid artery and anterolateral to the vertebral transverse foramen. No stenosis, occlusion, aneurysm, dissection, or other associated vascular abnormality was identified. The patient had no neurological symptoms attributable to the vascular variant. Although vertebral artery duplication is a rare congenital vascular anomaly, its identification in a young patient with suspected SLE undergoing evaluation for possible vasculitis represents an unusual clinical context. Recognition of this variant on CTA is important because its anomalous course may have implications for future cervical spine, vascular, or neurointerventional procedures. This case emphasizes the importance of careful evaluation of vertebral artery anatomy and accurate differentiation of congenital vascular variants from acquired vascular abnormalities.

items.title: Clinical experience with anti-interleukin-5 monoclonal antibodies in the treatment of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis is a rare disease whose standard treatment includes systemic glucocorticoids, bronchodilators, and immunosuppressive agents. Mepolizumab and benralizumab have recently emerged as therapeutic alternatives. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and treatment outcomes in real-world practice. This retrospective observational study included 29 adult patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis treated with mepolizumab and/or benralizumab at Hospital Universitario La Paz since 2017. Data were collected on oral glucocorticoid use, asthma therapies, immunosuppressive agents, eosinophil counts, and quality-of-life questionnaires to assess changes from baseline. The mean initial dose of prednisone was 15.4 mg per day. At six months, 60.9% of evaluable patients had reduced their dose, and at one year, glucocorticoids had been completely discontinued in 11 of 23 evaluable patients. Five patients continued on immunosuppressive therapy, while the rest discontinued it. Eosinophil counts decreased significantly at one year. Quality-of-life measures showed numerical improvements after one year of treatment. In this real-world cohort, treatment with mepolizumab or benralizumab was associated with reduced glucocorticoid use and eosinophil counts. items.title: Serum cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) NrCAM and P-Cadherin as novel biomarkers in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to identify novel serum biomarkers for lupus nephritis (LN) and evaluate their potential for improving diagnosis, monitoring disease activity, and understanding LN pathogenesis.MethodsA cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) antibody microarray was utilized to identify potential biomarkers of LN using serum samples from LN, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and healthy controls (HC). Differential expression analysis and LASSO regression identified CAM biomarkers in a discovery cohort, followed by ELISA validation in an independent, discovery cohort. Biomarker correlations with clinicopathological parameters were assessed, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed to examine the potential diagnostic utility.ResultsOf the 17 CAMs analyzed, serum NrCAM and P-Cadherin emerged as the most promising new biomarkers, significantly discriminating LN from HC. Serum NrCAM was found to differentiate between LN and HC ( p < 0.0001) as well as active LN (LNA) from inactive LN (LNI) ( p < 0.01) in the discovery cohort. Serum P-Cadherin, however, differentiated LN from both HC ( p < 0.0001) and CKD ( p < 0.001) and distinguished LNA from LNI ( p < 0.01). In a larger validation cohort, ROC analyses demonstrated strong diagnostic potential for both biomarkers, with AUC values of 0.92 and 0.82 for serum NrCAM and P-Cadherin, respectively. Significant correlations with SLEDAI, rSLEDAI, and histological indices further underscored their potential relevance to LN severity and activity. Interestingly, serum NrCAM and P-Cadherin are complementary in reflecting renal pathology changes including endocapillary hypercellularity, cellular crescents, glomerulosclerosis, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis.ConclusionSerum NrCAM and P-Cadherin show promise as non-invasive biomarkers for LN, offering potential utility in diagnosis and disease monitoring. Their ability to distinguish between disease states and correlate with clinical parameters highlights their potential to improve patient stratification and guide personalized treatment approaches in LN.

items.title: Spatial frequency domain imaging for assessment of skin fibrosis in systemic sclerosis: a prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis is an autoimmune disease with no approved skin-directed therapies. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) is the standard measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis, but it has limitations. There is an unmet need for a non-invasive skin outcome measure that is objective, biologically anchored to dermal fibrosis, and scalable for multicentre trials. We evaluated spatial frequency domain imaging (SFDI), a wide field, non-contact optical method as a systemic sclerosis skin outcome measure. This single-centre, prospective, cohort study was done at the Division of Rheumatology at the Boston Medical Center (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with systemic sclerosis fulfilling the 2013 American College of Rheumatology-European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria. Control participants were people aged 18 years or older without autoimmune disease or known skin pathology. For all participants, exclusion criteria included skin malignancy, wounds or rashes at SFDI measurement sites (dorsal hands, forearms, and fingers). Participants in the pilot phase completed one study visit with SFDI, mRSS assessment, and optional forearm biopsy. In the expanded protocol phase, participants had a baseline visit, with follow-up visits once every 3 months during the first year and once every 6 months thereafter for 3 years. At each study visit, SFDI, high-frequency ultrasound, and durometry were done in all participants, and mRSS was assessed in patients with systemic sclerosis. Optional forearm biopsy and blood collection was done at baseline in consenting participants. Main analyses assessed baseline associations of SFDI parameters (diffuse reflectance [R d ] and reduced scattering coefficient [μ s ']) with mRSS and correlations with histological features of skin involvement in forearm biopsies (dermal fibrosis, collagen content, myofibroblast staining, epidermal and dermal thickness, and additional histological features). Linear mixed-effects models were used for associations and Spearman models for correlations. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were not involved in the study design. Between Oct 17, 2019, and June 18, 2025, 54 patients with systemic sclerosis and 30 healthy control participants were enrolled across the pilot and expanded protocol phases. The final analysis included 49 participants with systemic sclerosis and 25 control participants; biopsy samples were obtained from 34 participants with systemic sclerosis and 16 control participants. 38 (78%) of 49 participants with systemic sclerosis were female, 11 (22%) were male, 34 (69%) were White, and mean age was 50 years (SD 16). 20 (80%) of 25 control participants were female, five (20%) were male, 14 (56%) were White, and mean age was 49 years (SD 14). R d and μ s ' were significantly lower in the systemic sclerosis cohort than in the control cohort across all mRSS strata, including sites where mRSS was 0. For each one-point increase in local mRSS there was a decrease in R d (β=-0·0028, 95% CI -0·0050 to -0·0006; p=0·014) and μ s ' (β=-0·0158, 95% CI -0·0314 to -0·0003; p=0·047). SFDI correlations were weak to moderate with mRSS (r ranged from -0·38 to -0·48) and moderate with histological fibrosis (r ranged from -0·34 to -0·52). SFDI provides an objective, non-invasive measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis that aligns with established clinical, imaging, and histological assessments. These findings support its potential as a quantitative outcome measure for evaluating skin disease in systemic sclerosis, consistent with Outcome Measures in Rheumatology principles. items.title: Exploration of the genetic architecture of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is a complex autoimmune disease with distinct clinical and serological subtypes. Previous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several susceptibility loci, particularly within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), but the broader genetic architecture and causal variants underlying AAV remain incompletely defined. We conducted a genome-wide association study including 2068 individuals with AAV and 3258 controls of European ancestry. The discovery cohort comprised a previously published GWAS dataset supplemented with newly recruited cases. Analyses were stratified by clinical (granulomatosis with polyangiitis [GPA] and microscopic polyangiitis [MPA]) and serological (proteinase 3-ANCA [PR3] and myeloperoxidase-ANCA [MPO]) subtypes. Findings were evaluated in an independent case cohort of 465 individuals. We performed conditional and joint analyses of the HLA region, functional fine-mapping, linkage disequilibrium score regression, and integrative multi-omics analyses to prioritise candidate causal variants and assess genetic correlations. We identified eight previously unreported loci and replicated four known loci associated with AAV at genome-wide significance. Within the HLA region, HLA-DPB1∗04 showed the strongest association with AAV, GPA, and PR3 subtypes, whereas HLA-DRB1∗04 was most strongly associated with MPO and MPA. Conditional analyses identified additional independent effects, including amino acid variation in HLA-DQA1. SNP-based heritability estimates indicated a substantial genetic contribution to AAV (h 2 = 0·40). Genetic correlation analyses revealed shared heritability with multiple traits, including celiac disease and hypothyroidism. Integrative analyses highlighted candidate genes, including HCG9 and PRTN3, and implicated protein interaction networks involving genes related to neutrophil biology. Protein-protein interaction analysis identified networks involving genes implicated in AAV risk, including PRTN3, AZU1, ELANE, and SERPINA1. These findings expand the genetic landscape of AAV and support a complex and heterogeneous genetic architecture involving both MHC and non-MHC loci. The integration of genetic association, functional annotation, and network analyses suggests that disease susceptibility is mediated through multiple biological pathways, including immune regulation and neutrophil function. These insights may inform future mechanistic studies, improved disease stratification, and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies. items.title: TREM2+ lung macrophages and serum soluble TREM2 in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease.
items.abstract: To characterise TREM2-expressing lung macrophage states in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis (DM)-associated interstitial lung disease (ILD) and to evaluate serum soluble TREM2 (sTREM2) as a biomarker. Public lung scRNA-seq data from a single anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD case and nine healthy donors were integrated. Serum sTREM2 was measured by ELISA in 25 newly diagnosed anti-MDA5+ DM patients and 15 matched healthy controls; 12-month follow-up samples were available for 19. Associations with ILD, laboratory indices and pulmonary function were analyzed. Exploratory scRNA-seq analysis suggests TREM2 was enriched in lung macrophages in a single anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD lung sample. Within this sample, TREM2+ macrophages showed higher interferon-response and M2 scores, lower M1 scores, and increased expression of profibrotic genes (SPP1, PLA2G7, FABP5 and PDGFA). In a bleomycin mouse model, TREM2+ Macrophages were significantly increased at day 7 and were surrounded by abundant profibrotic POSTN+CTHRC1+ myofibroblasts at day 21. Baseline serum sTREM2 was higher in anti-MDA5+ DM than controls (median 72.49 ng/mL [IQR 51.14-99.35] vs 31.39 ng/mL [22.10-43.74]; P < 0.0001) and highest in ILD (94.16 ng/mL [IQR 62.71-118.47]), but did not differ between RP-ILD and non-RP-ILD. Serum sTREM2 correlated with disease activity markers and inversely with %FVC and %DLco. At 12 months, sTREM2 decreased in stable/improved patients but increased in aggravated patients, but baseline sTREM2 did not predict aggravation. Serum sTREM2 is a candidate, non-invasive monitoring biomarker that reflects ILD severity and changes in parallel with the clinical course in anti-MDA5+ DM.

items.title: Lung ultrasound as part of a diagnostic algorithm to detect interstitial lung disease in rheumatoid arthritis patients at risk.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) affects 5-10% of patients with RA. While lung ultrasound (LUS) shows promise for RA-ILD detection, its role remains inconclusive. We aimed to assess its performance as a screening tool in at-risk RA patients. We made a cross-sectional study of RA patients, including i) individuals >50 years old with ≥1 risk factor for ILD, and ii) patients with new-onset respiratory symptoms. All patients underwent clinical examination, pulmonary function testing (PFT), LUS, and chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). LUS was considered abnormal in case of ≥5 total B-lines, and diagnostic accuracy was compared against HRCT, using a recent American Thoracic Society definition. We included 103 RA patients (73% women; mean age 63.4 years, median disease duration 7 years, 62% current or ever smokers, 68% seropositive for RF and/or ACPA). The majority (67 patients, 64.4%) reported no respiratory symptoms and had normal lung auscultation. According to ATS definition, 23 patients (22.3%) had ILD. Use of LUS for RA-ILD showed a sensitivity of 60.9% (95% CI: 40.8-77.8%), specificity of 63.7% (95% CI: 52.8-73.4%), and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 85% (95% CI: 73.9-91.9%). In regression and random forest analyses, LUS did not outperform DLCO for the prediction of RA-ILD. However, combination of negative LUS examination with normal DLCO essentially excluded RA-ILD (NPV 100%, 95%CI: 82-100%). Negative LUS in combination with normal DLCO reliably exclude ILD in at-risk RA patients, supporting its role in early RA-ILD detection.

items.title: Effectiveness, survival and prescription patterns of Janus kinase inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: results of a 5.9-year follow-up from the Italian Study Group of Early Arthritis (GISEA) registry.
items.abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKis) have emerged as a valuable treatment option for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Still, real-world data on their retention and prescription patterns are crucial, especially considering guideline updates. This study aimed to evaluate these aspects in a large Italian RA cohort. Patients with a diagnosis of RA enrolled in the Italian Study Group on Early Arthritis (GISEA) registry initiating JAKi therapy were included. Demographic and clinical characteristics, disease activity scores and treatment survival were assessed at baseline, at 6, 12, and 24 months and at last available visit or at drug discontinuation. Log-Rank tests and Cox regression analysis were employed to assess drugs survival and factors associated with discontinuation. Prescription patterns and patients selection were analysed across three periods reflecting key events in JAKi utilisation. 1303 patients were included. JAKi retention rates at 6, 12, and 24 months were 80.9%, 74.9%, and 61.1%, respectively. Glucocorticoid use, higher disease activity, and significant pain at baseline were associated with shorter retention. Conversely, first-line JAKi therapy after csDMARD failure was associated with longer retention. Prescription patterns shifted over time, with a trend towards earlier JAKi use among younger patients with established disease, and a more cautious approach following safety warnings, including reduced first-line use and less combination therapy. This large real-world study confirms the effectiveness of JAKis in RA, with valuable insights into factors influencing treatment survival and evolving prescription trends.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of glucocorticoids combined with mycophenolate mofetil versus methotrexate in IgG4-related disease: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: To compare the efficacy and safety of glucocorticoids (GCs) plus mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) versus methotrexate (MTX) in treatment-naive patients with IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). This retrospective cohort study included 154 treatment-naive patients with IgG4-RD. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 80 matched patients (40 per group) were analysed. Outcomes at 3, 6, and 12 months included complete response (CR), partial response (PR), overall response rate (ORR), clinical remission, treatment failure, relapse, and adverse events. False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction was applied for multiple comparisons in subgroup and repeated-measures analyses. Baseline characteristics were well balanced after matching. At 6 months, the MMF group showed higher ORR (92.5% vs. 72.5%, p=0.019) and PR (85.0% vs. 62.5%, p=0.022), although these differences did not retain significance after FDR correction (q=0.066 for both). At 12 months, MMF was superior in ORR (87.5% vs. 62.5%, p=0.010), CR (32.5% vs. 10.0%, p=0.014) and clinical remission rates (85.0% vs. 52.5%, p=0.002). Treatment failure was lower in the MMF group (2.5% vs. 25.0%, p=0.003). In the visceral subgroup, MMF yielded higher clinical remission (90.5% vs. 52.2%, p=0.005). Adverse events were more frequent in the MTX group (22.5% vs. 5.0%; unadjusted p=0.048; after FDR correction, q=0.336). Relapse rates were similar between groups. GCs plus MMF demonstrated better mid- to long-term efficacy and lower treatment failure than GCs plus MTX in this cohort, with potential benefits in patients with visceral involvement. These findings support MMF as a potential option for long-term maintenance therapy and warrant further prospective evaluation.

items.title: Machine learning models identify a distinct urinary metabolomic signature in children with non-systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
items.abstract: Despite advances in understanding the molecular mechanisms behind juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), reliable non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring remain limited. Urinary metabolomics offers a promising approach to investigate disease-specific metabolic alterations, especially in the paediatric setting. This exploratory study aimed to characterise the urinary metabolomic profile of children with non-systemic JIA with a machine learning-based approach. We conducted a cross-sectional study including 98 participants under 18 years of age (58 non-systemic JIA patients and 40 healthy controls). Urine samples were collected and analysed by targeted metabolomics. Feature selection was conducted using Boruta and recursive feature elimination (RFE). Supervised machine learning (ML) models, including logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and random forest (RF), were developed and evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. Univariate analysis did not reveal any statistically significant metabolites between groups after false discovery rate correction. However, a trend towards upregulation was observed in JIA patients for urinary glycine and long-chain acylcarnitines. Boruta and RFE identified a shared subset of informative features, which were used for classification modelling. The RF model achieved the best performance (AUC 0.989; 95% CI: 0.78-1.00), followed by LR (AUC 0.898; 95% CI: 0.78-1.00) and KNN (AUC 0.795; 95% CI: 0.71-0.99). A multivariate approach and supervised ML models revealed a subtle but biologically relevant urinary metabolomic signature in children with non-systemic JIA, leading to highly accurate patient classification. Given the exploratory nature of this research, further studies with larger and more stratified cohorts are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps activate lymphocytes in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: The aberrant activation of lymphocytes caused by autoantigens plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). A large number of autoantigens are released during the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), but their pathogenic mechanism in SLE has not been fully elucidated. We therefore investigated the role of NETs by activating lymphocytes in SLE. Peripheral venous blood samples from 58 patients with SLE and 54 healthy controls were included in this study, and the activated indicators of lymphocytes (HLA-DR and CD69) were analysed by flow cytometry. The NETs levels were quantified and their correlation with the levels of activated lymphocytes were analysed. Polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs) and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated via gradient density separation. The PMNs were stimulated using phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) to form NETs following incubation with autologous PBMCs. The activation of the lymphocytes was tested via flow cytometry. The elevated expression of HLA-DR and CD69 on CD4+ T and CD19+ B cells was observed in the patients with SLE and positively correlated with the NETs level (p<0.05). In contrast to the control group, the NETs group directly activated the CD4+ T and CD19+ B lymphocytes in vitro by increasing the expression of HLA-DR and CD69 (p<0.05). NETs induced the abnormal activation of T and B lymphocytes, which participated in the pathogenesis of SLE. This finding revealed the synergistic roles of innate immunity mediated by neutrophils and adaptive immunity mediated by lymphocytes.

items.title: A clinical model for identifying proliferative lupus nephritis: a multicenter study.
items.abstract: Proliferative lupus nephritis (PLN) is associated with poorer renal outcomes than non-proliferative lupus nephritis. Although kidney biopsy remains the gold standard for histologic classification, its use may be limited by invasiveness, contraindications, and limited healthcare access. We aimed to develop and externally validate a noninvasive model for identifying PLN. In this multicenter retrospective study, 443 patients with biopsy-confirmed lupus nephritis from five centers were included. The development cohort comprised 337 patients from center A, and the external validation cohort included 106 patients from centers B to E. Candidate predictors were screened using univariable analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, followed by multivariable logistic regression to construct the final nomogram. Internal validation was performed using 5-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. The final model incorporated seven predictors, namely lymphocyte percentage, hematuria, leukocyturia, estimated glomerular filtration rate, uric acid, anti-dsDNA positivity, and C3. The model showed good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.852 in the development cohort and 0.895 in the external validation cohort. Calibration was acceptable in both cohorts, and decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical utility. We developed and externally validated a noninvasive clinical model based on routinely available clinical variables for identifying PLN. This model may provide a practical tool for risk stratification and support clinical evaluation in patients with lupus nephritis.
