items.title: Donor-aware integrative single-cell analysis distinguishes consistent memory B-cell programmes from donor-sensitive state boundaries in untreated rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics resolves immune-cell heterogeneity, but whether cluster boundaries or coordinated programmes are the more transferable unit across donors remains uncertain. We reanalyzed 14,414 circulating memory B cells from four untreated rheumatoid arthritis donors. Harmony increased mean local donor entropy from 0.506 to 0.912, while original labels showed only moderate agreement with uncorrected and Harmony reclustering (adjusted Rand indices 0.508 and 0.473). Conditional label permutations and analyses based on pan-B-centred residuals or state-marker genes supported donor-level consistency for most major states, but identified C3-PECAM1 and the rare C10-IFN state as weakly specific or quality-control-sensitive. In training-only donor-held-out transfer, accuracy was 66.0-70.5% and adjusted Rand index was 0.432-0.525, indicating partial transfer rather than independent state recovery. Removal of DoubletFinder-predicted doublets preserved 15-20 of each state's top 20 pseudobulk markers and did not change programme rank order across states. Rank-based UCell scores agreed with AddModuleScore in both datasets. In an independent cohort of 5,725 memory B cells from 34 donors, adapted programme scores could be quantified, but no disease-activity or serological association remained significant after correction; treatment and unavailable disease-duration data limited clinical interpretation. These results distinguish recurrent donor-level transcriptional structure from analysis-sensitive state boundaries and support programme-level interpretation without claiming independent cell-state validation or biomarker utility.

items.title: Performance of the Expanded Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Score for Rheumatoid Arthritis: An External Validation in the BRASS Registry.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular (CV) disease occurs more frequently in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) than in the general population and is difficult to predict. The expanded risk score for RA (ERS-RA) has demonstrated good discrimination and calibration in prior studies, but additional external validation studies are needed to understand clinical utility. Data from a single center RA registry was integrated with electronic health records (EHR) and linked to Medicare/Medicaid administrative claims data. A less restrictive CV outcome was defined as an event identified in any of the three data sources (questionnaires/EHR/claims), and a more restrictive outcome included events in EHR and claims. External validation of the ERS-RA examined model discrimination and calibration. The longitudinal RA registry has 1,332 participants aged 20-80 years without prior evidence of CVD, followed for a mean of 6.8 years. The mean age was 54 years and 84% were female. We observed 164 (12.3%) and 69 (5.2%) participants with a CV event with the less and more restrictive CV definitions, respectively. The mean ERS-RA predicted score was 7.1%, and 424 (32%) participants had a predictive score ≥7.5%. We observed c-statistics of 0.66 (95% CI 0.62-0.71; less restrictive) and 0.80 (95% CI 0.76-0.85; more restrictive). The ERS-RA also demonstrated good calibration, with better performance for the more restrictive CV event definition. The ERS-RA demonstrated good discrimination and calibration for CV risk prediction in an external validation RA cohort. It also highlights the importance of using multiple sources of data to find CV events in a non-CV registry.

items.title: Disseminated Herpes Simplex Virus Infection Presenting With Cytopenias in a Patient With Untreated Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection is an uncommon but serious condition, typically seen in immunocompromised hosts. Cytopenias, including neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, are rare manifestations, particularly in patients not actively receiving immunosuppressive therapy. We report a 75-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), previously on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone, who presented with painful oral and genital ulcers, mucositis, and rapidly progressive bicytopenia (neutropenia and thrombocytopenia). Her recent brief reinitiation of methotrexate prompted evaluation for drug-induced cytopenias; however, methotrexate levels were undetectable. Extensive infectious, nutritional, rheumatologic, and hematologic workup revealed HSV positivity from oral and inguinal ulcers. Bone marrow biopsy showed no evidence of hematologic malignancy or aplasia. She was treated with intravenous acyclovir, leading to clinical improvement and recovery of blood counts. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of cytopenias in patients with autoimmune diseases. While methotrexate toxicity and Felty's syndrome were initially considered, the clinical trajectory and lack of supportive findings redirected focus to infectious causes. Disseminated HSV infection causing cytopenias is rare and often overlooked in immunocompetent or intermittently immunosuppressed patients. In this patient, immune dysregulation due to underlying RA and advanced age likely contributed to HSV dissemination and bone marrow suppression. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for disseminated HSV in patients with autoimmune diseases presenting with mucocutaneous lesions and cytopenias, even in the absence of significant immunosuppressive therapy. Prompt recognition and antiviral therapy are critical to prevent complications and improve outcomes.

items.title: Pulmonary Embolism Revealing an Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Venous thromboembolism presents a rare clinical manifestation of Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with polyangiitis. We present a case of pulmonary embolism associated with Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) systemic manifestations in a 26-year-old Tunisian female patient. She presented with dyspnea and blood hypereosinophilia. Blood tests revealed elevated D-dimer levels. Lung scintigraphy (V/Q-scan) revealed pulmonary artery embolism in the right lung. The Computed Tomography (CT) image showed circumferential wall thickness of the lower mediastinal oesophagus and gastroesophageal junction. The chest scan also showed multiple pulmonary infiltrates with a ground-glass appearance localized in the apex of the posterior segment of the right upper lobe. The CT scan of the sinuses showed circumferential thickening of the maxillary sinus. Based on the 2022 ACR/EULAR diagnosis criteria, the patient was diagnosed with Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis. After one month of anti-vitamin K treatment, a spirometry showed an obstructive pattern. The patient underwent methylprednisolone pulses, followed by oral corticosteroids, which were slowly tapered concomitantly with a cyclophosphamide regimen. A marked improvement of the spirometry parameters was achieved. Clinicians should be vigilant in the diagnostic and therapeutic management of Pulmonary Embolism (PE) during the active phase of EGPA to establish adequate follow-up procedures.

items.title: A3 Adenosine Receptor in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Friend or Foe? A Key Mediator of Different Signaling Pathways.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease that has heterogeneous clinical manifestations. The A3 Adenosine Receptor (A3AR), a protein implicated in numerous inflammatory pathways, is overexpressed in patients with RA. The available preclinical and clinical literature about A3AR signaling in RA was reviewed, and published data on its molecular pathways, immunomodulatory functions, and role in synovial fibroblasts were searched. Studies exploring A3AR agonists and their mechanistic interactions with NF-κB and p53 pathways were also reviewed. The mechanisms in which the A3AR is involved in alleviating inflammatory status resulting from alterations in transcriptional activity of the nuclear factor kappa B-light- chain-enhancer of activated inflammatory cells (NF-κB) in RA and the clinical and preclinical studies working on A3AR agonists alongside the apoptosis process by interacting with the p53 expression level. In contrast, we explained that the canonical and non-canonical pathways for A3AR, which may lead to worsening inflammation, were detailed. The implication of A3AR in the worsening of destructive effects on RA synovium in cases of hypoxia, as well as the consequences of low oxygen levels on FLSs, was detailed. In conclusion, we hypothesized that the overexpressed A3AR could provide the activation of Ras, leading to the inflammatory and senescent phenotype of FLSs during the pathological processes in RA.

items.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Identifies TTN as a Potential Diagnostic Marker for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with heterogeneous clinical manifestations, and its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. To identify core genes associated with RA and evaluate their diagnostic utility, with an emphasis on immune relevance and causality. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene coexpression network analysis were used to prioritize hub genes. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses supported biological interpretation. A nomogram and receiver operating characteristic analysis were used to evaluate diagnostic performance, and immune cell infiltration was analyzed to identify immune-associated core genes. The causal effect of titin on the risk of RA was estimated using genome-wide association study data and two-sample Mendelian randomization. Validation was conducted in independent public transcriptomic datasets and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of synovial tissue. Titin (TTN) was prioritized as an RA-associated core gene and demonstrated favorable diagnostic performance. TTN expression was consistently higher in RA than in controls across validation datasets. Public external validation datasets supported increased TTN expression in RA, and scRNA-seq analysis suggested enrichment of TTN expression in synovial T cells. Mendelian randomization supported a causal association between genetically predicted TTN and RA risk. Collectively, evidence from bulk transcriptomics, immune cell infiltration profiling, single-cell localization, external validation, and genetic inference supports TTN as a previously underexplored candidate RA-associated biomarker with potential immune relevance. These findings extend current RA biomarker discovery by linking diagnostic performance with immune context and genetic support. Further mechanistic studies are needed to clarify whether TTN is involved in RA immunopathology or reflects inflammation-related tissue remodeling. Integrative analyses identify TTN as a potential RA-associated diagnostic biomarker requiring further experimental and clinical validation. Further studies are needed to clarify its mechanistic role and clinical utility in RA.

items.title: The Usefulness of White Blood Cell Inflammatory Parameters in Children With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: To evaluate the utility of novel parameters related to immune cell activation, known as white blood cell parameters of inflammation (WBC-IP), as biomarkers of disease activity in childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (cSLE) and compare their performance with conventional markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and procalcitonin (PCT). We conducted a cross-sectional analysis, including patients with cSLE with active disease (n = 43), remission (n = 31), and healthy controls (n = 112). In a separate longitudinal cohort, patients with active cSLE at baseline were reassessed after four to six weeks and when achieving inactive disease. WBC-IP was measured in dipotassium EDTA-anticoagulated tubes using the Sysmex XN-Series analyzer. Associations with SLEDAI-2K, clinical SLEDAI-2K, and physician global assessment (PGA) scores were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Diagnostic performance for distinguishing active disease from remission was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Significant alterations in neutrophil- and lymphocyte-related parameters were observed across disease states. The proportion of immature granulocytes (IG%) correlated most strongly with the SLEDAI-2K (r s  = 0.51), clinical SLEDAI-2K (r s  = 0.50), and PGA (r s  = 0.57; all P < 0.0001) and showed comparable associations with ESR, CRP, and PCT. Longitudinal changes in IG%, neutrophil reactivity intensity, and lymphocyte complexity indices paralleled improvements in disease activity. IG% best discriminated active cSLE among WBC-IP (AUC 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.83-0.98; cutoff >0.35, sensitivity 81.4%, specificity 87.1%), whereas ESR demonstrated the highest AUC among conventional markers (AUC 0.92, 95% CI 0.85-0.99). Among the WBC-IP evaluated, IG% showed the strongest association with disease activity and demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of ESR, suggesting it may represent a potential biomarker of disease activity. Further validation in independent cohorts is warranted.

items.title: Autophagy - related protein 5: A promising biomarker for disease activity and treatment response in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Existing biomarkers are often insufficient for adequately tracking treatment outcomes in lupus nephritis (LN). Growing evidence points to a significant role of autophagy in LN pathogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate circulating levels of autophagy-related protein 5 (ATG5) alongside its immunohistochemical expression in kidney biopsy from LN patients, and to examine its utility as a diagnostic indicator and predictor of therapeutic response. This pilot prospective research enrolled 31 patients with active LN and 9 age and sex matched normal controls. Immunohistochemical evaluation of ATG5 expression was conducted on renal biopsy specimens collected before the commencement of medication, while blood ATG5 levels were evaluated in all subjects. Serial serum ATG5 evaluations were performed at 3-month and 6-month intervals after the initiation of therapy. Circulating ATG5 levels were significantly decreased in LN patients relative to controls (cut-off ≤312.3 ng/l; AUC=0.943; sensitivity 100%; specificity 88.9%). Renal tissue ATG5 expression was detected in 96.7% of patients; strong expression identified in 87.1% using summation scoring (score >3) and in 58.1% using multiplication scoring (score >8). A biopsy summation score ≤6 predicted treatment response with AUC of 0.88, sensitivity 69.57% and 100% specificity. Treatment was associated with significant ATG5 recovery over 6 months (p < 0.001), with responders demonstrating lower biopsy scores and greater serum ATG5 improvement versus non-responders (p=0.004, p=0.009, respectively). Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) treatment yielded superior outcomes compared to cyclophosphamide (p=0.042). The summation and multiplication scores of ATG5 exhibited a negative correlation with serum ATG5 after six months (p < 0.026 and p < 0.018, respectively). In conclusion, ATG5 represents a valuable autophagy-related biomarker in LN, offering reliable predictive utility for treatment outcomes. Lower intra-renal ATG5 expression scores are associated with favourable therapeutic responses, particularly in patients receiving MMF.

items.title: Causes of hospitalization in systemic lupus erythematosus patients at a tertiary care center: insights from South Asia.
items.abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) often require hospitalization due to disease flares, infections, or other complications. While studies from high-income countries consistently report flares and infections as leading causes, data from South Asia remain limited. This study aimed to identify the leading causes of hospitalization and describe the associated clinical outcomes of patients admitted to a tertiary care center in Nepal. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at the B.P. Koirala Institute of Health Sciences, Nepal, including all eligible SLE patients (aged >16 years and diagnosed for >3 months using the SLICC 2012 criteria) from November 2023 to November 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were collected. Reasons for hospitalization and in-hospital outcomes were recorded. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Sixty-four patients were included; 93.8% were female, with a mean age of 32.4 ± 11.1 years. SLE flare was the most common cause of hospitalization (56.3%), followed by infection (20.3%). Renal flare accounted for the most flare-related admissions (39.1%), while urinary tract infection and acute undifferentiated fever were the leading infections. Nearly half of the patients (46.9%) were not on any immunosuppressive therapy at admission, and hydroxychloroquine use was suboptimal (67.2%). The mean hospital stay was 5.3 ± 3.0 days. Most patients were discharged in stable condition (95.3%); one required ICU transfer, and one died (1.6%). Renal flares and infections were the most frequent causes of hospitalization in this South Asian SLE cohort, highlighting the need for early recognition and management.

items.title: Xinfeng capsule regulates pyroptosis and ameliorates cardiac fibrosis in rheumatoid arthritis through lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways.
items.abstract: Xinfeng capsule (XFC) is a traditional Chinese medicinal compound that has been used clinically for several years to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-related cardiac dysfunction. Nevertheless, the mechanism through which XFC treats RA-induced cardiac impairment remains unclear. This study investigates the mechanism by which XFC-containing serum regulates pyroptosis and ameliorates cardiac fibrosis in RA through the lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways. A cardiac fibrosis model using human myocardial cells was established to study lncRNA GAS5, miR-21, TLR4, and NLRP3 expressions. Immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, WB, dual-luciferase assay, CCK-8, flow cytometry, electron microscopy, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay were used to analyze various cellular processes and protein levels. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) releases were also analyzed. The mRNA and protein expressions of multiple genes were assessed. The optimal intervention conditions for AC16 cells were determined as follows: 20 µg/L for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) for 24 h, and 10% for XFC. In the LPS group, cell viability decreased, LDH release increased, and there was an elevation in pro-inflammatory cytokines and pyroptosis-related protein expression. GAS5 expression was reduced, while TLR4, ROS, and miR-21 showed increased levels compared to the NC group. GAS5 acted as an inhibitor by sponging miR-21. Conversely, XFC-containing serum, GAS5 overexpression, and miR-21 inhibition exhibited positive effects - enhancing cell viability, preventing LDH and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and reducing pyroptosis and fibrosis-related protein levels. XFC can inhibit cellular pyroptosis, reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, and improve RA cardiac fibrosis via lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways.

items.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Vicatia thibetica De Boiss. in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Associated Multi-Pathway Modulation In Vivo.
items.abstract: Vicatia thibetica de Boiss. (VTDB) is not only used as an important Tibetan medicine but is also consumed as a common wild vegetable. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive destruction of cartilage and bone. VTDB is recorded in the Four Medical Classics for treating "Huang-Shui," a condition resembling RA. To preliminarily investigate its potential therapeutic basis, VTDB and its polarity-based fractions were evaluated for their effects against RA. The chemical constituents of VTDB-TE were profiled using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap MS/MS, and network pharmacology analysis predicted possible involvement of the PI3K/Akt and JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathways. Among the tested fractions, VTDB-nBuOH exhibited the most pronounced pharmacological activity in the collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model. VTDB-nBuOH treatment was associated with reduced paw swelling, lower serum levels of rheumatoid factor (RF) and C-reactive protein (CRP), and improved synovial histopathology. The treatment was also associated with reduced levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and alterations in the levels of proteins associated with PI3K/Akt, JAK2/STAT3, and the downstream IKK/IκB/NF-κB axis. Additionally, VTDB-nBuOH treatment was associated with a shift in macrophage polarization markers toward an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype, suggesting a possible restoration of the M1/M2 balance within the joint microenvironment. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed VTDB-nBuOH treatment-associated changes in gut microbial composition, including enrichment of certain beneficial genera and reduction of some pathogenic taxa. Proteomic analysis also pointed to the PI3K/Akt pathway as a potential node of interest. Collectively, these correlative findings suggest that VTDB-nBuOH may alleviate synovial inflammation and cartilage and bone damage through multi-pathway modulation, though further mechanistic studies are needed to establish causality. VTDB-nBuOH shows preliminary promise for further investigation as a potential candidate for RA treatment.

items.title: Lipid and immune profiles in children with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis: a case-control study with paired longitudinal comparison of disease activity.
items.abstract: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (SoJIA) lacks specific biomarkers for objective disease activity assessment. Conventional inflammatory markers have limited accuracy for monitoring disease fluctuation. Few studies have integrated lipid metabolic and immune parameters to support SoJIA activity assessment, underscoring the need for simple and efficient biomarker combinations. This study aims to characterize differences in immune parameters between children with active SoJIA and healthy controls; compare the lipid profiles among children with active SoJIA, the same children in remission, and healthy controls; and explore the ability of these parameters to discriminate between disease states. This single-center retrospective case-control study included 63 treatment-naive children newly diagnosed SoJIA (PRINTO 2018 criteria). Remission was defined by ACR/PRINTO criteria, with normal C-reactive protein (CRP) ≤10 mg/L and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) ≤20 mm/h. Forty age- and sex-matched healthy children served as controls. Blood was collected after an overnight fast. Immune, cytokine, lipid, and inflammatory markers were measured using standardized clinical laboratory procedures. Cellular immune markers (CD3⁺, CD4⁺, CD8⁺, CD16⁺CD56⁺, CD19⁺), cytokines [interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-10 (IL-10), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R)], humoral immune indicators [immunoglobulin G (IgG), immunoglobulin M (IgM), complement component 3 (C3), complement component 4 (C4)], lipid parameters, CRP, and ESR were measured. The atherogenic index (AI) was calculated. Compared with healthy controls, children with active SoJIA had significantly higher levels of C3, C4, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α, CRP, and ESR; higher proportions of CD3⁺ and CD4⁺ T cells; and lower B cells than controls (all P<0.05). Both active and remission patients had lipid abnormalities (lower HDL-C, higher TG and AI), more pronounced during active disease. Total cholesterol (TC) was elevated only in the active group (all P<0.05). Joint swelling and fever were more frequent during active disease than during remission (P<0.05). A CRP + IL-6 + AI model distinguished active SoJIA from controls with exploratory ability (73.0% sensitivity, 95.0% specificity). AI + TG distinguished active from remission disease (area under the curve =0.8650). Active SoJIA shows prominent immune-inflammatory dysregulation and lipid abnormalities that partially improve with remission. The CRP + IL-6 + AI model showed exploratory ability to distinguish active SoJIA from health, whereas AI alone demonstrated exploratory potential for evaluating disease activity. Adding TG did not significantly improve performance (DeLong test, P=0.80). As only healthy controls were included without disease-mimic groups and models lacked independent validation, these findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot support clinical differential diagnosis. Prospective multicenter studies that include appropriate disease-control groups and independent validation cohorts are needed.

items.title: Thymic CT attenuation score in SAPHO syndrome: a comparative study with rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and healthy controls.
items.abstract: SAPHO syndrome is a rare autoinflammatory/autoimmune overlap disorder whose thymic imaging characteristics remain unexplored. This study evaluated thymic CT attenuation scores in patients with SAPHO syndrome compared with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis (AS), and healthy controls (HC). This retrospective study included 180 patients with SAPHO syndrome, 60 with RA, 60 with AS, and 180 HC, all aged ≥30 years. Thymic attenuation was assessed using a 4-point scale (0-3) and CT attenuation values in Hounsfield units (HU). Higher attenuation was defined as score ≥2. Subgroup analyses were performed by sex and age (<45 vs ≥45 years). The prevalence of higher thymic attenuation differed significantly among the four groups (P<0.001), with proportions of 31.1% in SAPHO, 25.0% in RA, 8.3% in AS, and 10.6% in HC. Post hoc analyses of the ordinal attenuation score and CT attenuation values showed higher values in SAPHO and RA than in AS and HC, whereas SAPHO and RA did not differ significantly from each other. This pattern appeared most pronounced among women aged <45 years, in whom higher attenuation was observed in 54.3% of SAPHO and 47.8% of RA patients, compared with 19.2% of HC and 3.8% of AS patients. Within the SAPHO group, higher attenuation was associated with female sex (85.7% vs 68.5%, P = 0.015) and younger age (median 37.5 vs 44 years, P<0.001). Thymic CT attenuation was higher in SAPHO and RA, particularly among women aged <45 years, whereas AS showed findings similar to HC. Increased thymic attenuation may represent a potential imaging phenotype associated with SAPHO syndrome and RA. Further longitudinal and pathological studies are needed to clarify its biological significance.

items.title: Predictive biomarkers for precision treatment in rheumatoid arthritis: are we there yet?
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting approximately 1% of the global population and is associated with a substantial reduction in both life expectancy and quality of life. Although current treatments, primarily disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, have been shown to suppress inflammation, clinical responses vary widely between individuals, reflecting the heterogeneity of the disease. Consequently, identifying reliable biomarkers to predict therapeutic response has become a key priority for improving clinical management. In this focused review, we summarise recent advances in the discovery of predictive biomarkers for RA and compare their reported specificity and sensitivity using published data. We also highlight key limitations in the existing literature that undermine reproducibility in this field. Coordinated efforts across the rheumatology community to address these challenges will be essential to translate biomarker research into personalised treatment strategies for RA.

items.title: Circulating angiogenic T cells as potential immune-vascular biomarkers associated with disease activity in axial spondyloarthritis.
items.abstract: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease associated with persistent systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Angiogenic T cells (Tang cells), defined as CD3 + CD31 + CD184 + T cells, are specialized immune cells involved in vascular repair and endothelial homeostasis, but their clinical relevance in axSpA remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize circulating Tang cells in axSpA and evaluate their potential as immune-vascular biomarkers of disease activity. Peripheral blood samples were obtained from patients with axSpA stratified by disease activity and from healthy controls. Circulating Tang cells and their phenotypic subsets were quantified using flow cytometry. Clinical characteristics, disease activity indices (ASDAS and BASDAI), inflammatory markers, and immunometabolic parameters were collected. Correlation analyses, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to assess the clinical significance of Tang cells in relation to axSpA disease activity. Tang cell frequency and absolute count were significantly decreased in active axSpA (median 16.40% [11.97%-25.65%]; 195.82 [135.07-322.53] cells/µL) compared with stable axSpA (32.11% [24.62%-42.33%]; 442.89 [306.48-633.02]) and healthy controls (32.23% [26.57%-43.87%]; 437.95 [293.73-507.95]) (all P  < 0.001). Tang cell frequency showed a positive correlation with CD14 + HLA-DR + monocyte proportions (Spearman r = 0.537, P  < 0.001) and an inverse correlation with BASDAI scores (Spearman r = -0.548, P  < 0.001). Multivariable regression analysis revealed that circulating Tang cell frequency remained independently and inversely associated with active disease status (OR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.79 - 0.95, P  = 0.002) after adjustment for traditional inflammatory markers including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). In addition, circulating Tang cells showed satisfactory discriminatory ability to distinguish active axSpA from stable axSpA (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.831). Circulating angiogenic T cells are inversely associated with disease activity in axSpA and represent a novel immune-vascular biomarker that is not redundant with traditional inflammatory parameters. These findings provide a clinical immunophenotypic framework highlighting altered vascular repair-immune interactions in axSpA and support further functional studies to clarify the functional role of Tang cells in disease pathogenesis.

items.title: Sanguinarine ameliorates rheumatoid arthritis by activating the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway to induce apoptosis and suppress inflammation in fibroblast-like synoviocytes.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with progressive joint damage, functional disability and systemic comorbidity. Available therapies are not satisfactory, including low rates of remission and about 30% of patients with poor response to first-line treatment. Thus, more effective therapeutic strategies are urgently needed. Sanguinarine, a benzophenanthridine alkaloid primarily isolated from Sanguinaria canadensis and other members of the Papaveraceae family, has been documented to possess notable anti-bacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anti-neoplastic properties. Nevertheless, its potential utility as a targeted therapeutic modality for RA has yet to be systematically investigated. Here, we demonstrate that sanguinarine can effectively ameliorate the development of adjuvant-induced arthritis in rats and decrease arthritis scores, attenuate the inflammatory response, and prevent bone and joint damage. Flow cytometry and ELISA both confirmed its anti-inflammatory activity, reducing the levels of PGE2, TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6. In human fibroblast-like synoviocytes from RA patients (HFLS-RA), sanguinarine triggered cell apoptosis accompanied by elevated intracellular ROS, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential and activation of caspase-3, and activated the Hippo/YAP pathway both in vitro and in vivo . These results suggest that sanguinarine ameliorates RA by activation of the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway to induce apoptosis and suppress inflammation, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic candidate for RA.

items.title: Eculizumab in rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis: a case-series report.
items.abstract: To describe the clinical outcomes and safety profile of eculizumab as adjunctive therapy in a case series of patients with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) due to anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) disease and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV). We reported 7 patients with AAV and 5 patients with anti-GBM disease who presented to our center between March 2025 and January 2026. All patients received eculizumab (900 mg, 1-4 doses) in addition to standard immunosuppressive therapy. Serum creatinine (Scr), urinary red blood cell (uRBC) count, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR), and dialysis dependence were assessed at baseline and at 3 months. Adverse events were monitored throughout follow-up. In AAV patients, mean Scr decreased from 407.38 μmol/L to 231.27 μmol/L ( p = 0.025), mean uRBC from 384.27/μL to 68.75/μL ( p = 0.033), and mean UPCR from 2.20 g/g to 1.64 g/g ( p = 0.179) at the 3rd month. In anti-GBM patients, mean Scr declined from 575.07 μmol/L to 263.80 μmol/L ( p  = 0.024), mean uRBC from 1648.60/μL to 461.92/μL ( p  = 0.132), and mean UPCR from 10.88 g/g to 3.75 g/g ( p  = 0.126). At baseline, 6 patients required renal replacement therapy, and after treatment, 4 became dialysis-independent. One AAV patient progressed to hemodialysis, and one anti-GBM patient remained dialysis-dependent. All anti-GBM antibodies and MPO-ANCA (except one patient) seroconverted to negative at month 3. During follow-up, only one case of COVID-19 infection and one oral ulcer were recorded; no severe infections occurred. In this descriptive case series, we observed trends toward improved renal function and hematuria at 3 months in patients with severe RPGN who received eculizumab in addition to standard immunosuppression, with earlier initiation and milder baseline renal impairment appearing to correlate with more favorable outcomes. Nevertheless, the lack of a control group and the marked interpatient variability in baseline characteristics and concomitant therapies preclude any conclusion regarding a causal effect of eculizumab. Instead, these data serve as real-world observations that can generate hypotheses for future studies. Definitive evidence on the efficacy and safety of eculizumab in RPGN must await larger, prospective, controlled investigations.

items.title: Immune profiling of anti-SSA-positive at-risk individuals reveals increased type I IFN activity preceding lymphocyte abnormalities in Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Identifying immune features that distinguish asymptomatic autoantibody-positive at-risk individuals from patients with established autoimmune disease is key to understanding the evolution from autoreactivity to established autoimmune disease. This study investigated immune characteristics of anti-SSA-positive at-risk individuals, including pregnant women, compared with patients with Sjögren's disease (SjD) and healthy donors (HDs). Peripheral blood samples were obtained from asymptomatic anti-SSA-positive women (at-risk individuals; n = 7, including two ongoing pregnancies with congenital heart block [CHB] and one woman with a prior CHB pregnancy), patients with SjD (n = 10), and age- and sex-matched HDs (n = 21; median age 35.1 years; 100% female). T- and B-cell subsets and IFN signaling molecules, including STAT1, phosphorylated STAT1 (pSTAT1), STAT2, IRF1, and IRF9, were analyzed by flow cytometry. In addition, circulating IFN subtypes were quantified in available plasma samples using the NULISA platform. At-risk individuals showed lower ANA and rheumatoid factor titers and lacked anti-SSB autoantibodies compared with patients with SjD. At-risk individuals had B-cell distributions similar to HDs, whereas patients with SjD showed a typical increase in naïve B cells and reduced pre-switched and switched memory B-cell frequencies, together with increased CD8+ T-cell frequencies and a non-significant trend toward reduced double-negative T-cell frequencies. At-risk individuals also showed significantly increased IFN activity, reflected by Siglec-1 (CD169) expression on CD14+ monocytes, compared with HDs, while levels tended to be lower than in patients with SjD. Two of three women with a current or previous CHB pregnancy had the highest Siglec-1 levels within the at-risk group. Cytokine profiling revealed a stage-associated IFN pattern, with IFN-α1 and IFN-ω already increased in at-risk individuals, whereas IFN-γ, IFN-β1, and type III IFNs showed a trend toward higher levels in established SjD. Intracellular STAT1 expression was elevated across CD19+ B-cell subsets in at-risk individuals compared with HDs, but was generally less pronounced than in SjD. IRF9 was also increased in B-cell subsets from at-risk individuals and patients with SjD compared with HDs. Similar findings were observed in CD3+ T-cell subsets, where STAT1 and IRF9 expression were elevated in at-risk individuals compared with HDs and were largely comparable to levels observed in patients with SjD. Our data suggest that increased type I IFN activity and IFN-associated signaling in T- and B-cell subsets are already present in anti-SSA-positive at-risk individuals. In contrast, altered B- and T-cell homeostasis was restricted to established SjD, indicating progression from autoreactivity toward overt autoimmune disease.

items.title: Efficacy, mechanisms, and influence factors of small molecule targeted therapy in treating rheumatoid arthritis: a multi-dimensional clinical, immunological, and ultrasonographic study.
items.abstract: Targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (tsDMARDs) show promise for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but multi-dimensional efficacy evaluation needs further study. This study aimed to comprehensively assess tsDMARDs' efficacy in RA and explore factors linked to treatment response. 123 consecutive active RA patients treated with tsDMARDs for ≥6 months at Suzhou Ninth People's Hospital (January 2023-December 2024) were retrospectively analyzed; 120 were included after exclusions. Clinical efficacy was appraised using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP), Clinical Disease Activity Index (CDAI), American College of Rheumatology 20/50/70 (ACR20/50/70), and the overall effective rate. Immunological parameters included erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA). Musculoskeletal ultrasound parameters consisted of synovial hypertrophy score assessed by gray-scale ultrasound (GSUS) and synovial vascularity grade assessed by power Doppler ultrasound (PDUS). Correlations between parameters were analyzed, and multivariate logistic regression pinpointed independent risk factors of favorable therapeutic response. Among 120 patients, patients were stratified into effective (n = 78) and non-effective (n = 42) groups, with comparable baseline characteristics (all P > 0.05). After 6 months, the effective group showed significantly greater improvements in DAS28-CRP, CDAI, ESR, CRP, RF, ACPA, GSUS, and PDUS (all P < 0.001). Positive correlations were present between immunological/ultrasound parameters and disease activity scores. Multivariate logistic regression identified reduced PDUS signal, lower CRP, and improved DAS28-CRP as independent predictors of favorable response. tsDMARDs effectively improve joint symptoms, reduce disease activity, and enhance articular function in RA patients, potentially supporting personalized therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Case Report: IgG4-related lung disease.
items.abstract: Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a systemic immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition, distinct from classical autoimmune disorders, that can affect multiple organs. Pulmonary involvement often presents with non-specific clinical and radiographic features, contributing to high rates of misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. Here, we report a rare case of IgG4-related lung disease (IgG4-RLD) to enhance clinical awareness. A 71-year-old female presented with cough. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed an irregular soft tissue mass in the right middle lobe. All autoantibodies tested were negative, and the serum IgG4 level was within the normal range. The patient showed no response to anti-infective and antitussive therapy, with follow-up CT confirming lesion enlargement. A CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy was subsequently performed. Histopathology demonstrated infiltration of numerous lymphocytes and plasma cells, along with scattered neutrophils. Immunohistochemistry showed a ratio of IgG4-positive to IgG-positive plasma cells of approximately 42%, and demonstrated approximately 30 IgG4-positive plasma cells per high-power field (HPF). The diagnosis of IgG4-RLD was established based on the 2019 ACR/EULAR International Classification Criteria for IgG4-RD. The patient was subsequently treated with oral prednisone, which led to complete resolution of the cough and near-complete regression of the pulmonary lesion.

items.title: Anti-GBM disease shortly after clinically presumed ANCA-associated vasculitis in an 85-year-old patient: a case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Sequential emergence of anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) disease after anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) is rare. An 85-year-old woman presented with fever, edema, elevated myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA, mild urinary abnormalities, markedly elevated urinary tubular injury markers, and negative serum anti-GBM antibodies measured by chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassay. Renal biopsy was not performed because of advanced age, severe dementia, antiplatelet therapy, and the family's preference for non-invasive management. She was clinically presumed to have AAV and achieved apparent clinical remission with prednisolone alone, although MPO-ANCA remained positive. However, 2.5 months after the initial AAV diagnosis, she developed rapidly progressive kidney failure requiring dialysis, accompanied by severe hematuria, increased proteinuria, urinary casts, and markedly elevated anti-GBM antibodies. Clinically diagnosed anti-GBM disease was treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy, prednisolone, plasma exchange, and hemodialysis. Although renal recovery was not achieved, anti-GBM antibodies became negative, and she remained clinically stable on maintenance hemodialysis for over 4 years while receiving low-dose prednisolone. This case suggests that anti-GBM disease can emerge shortly after apparent clinical remission of AAV. ANCA-mediated GBM injury and age-related GBM changes may contribute to subsequent anti-GBM autoimmunity, although these mechanisms remain hypothetical in this patient. Prompt anti-GBM antibody testing should be considered when a rapid, unexplained decline in kidney function occurs during or after AAV treatment.

items.title: Endoscopic resolution of esophageal varices in a patient with IgG4-related disease: a case report.
items.abstract: IgG4-related pancreatitis is a complex and multiorgan disease that can mimic pancreatic malignancy. Corticosteroids are the first-line therapy, but their use may not be an option for patients with metabolic comorbidities, such as diabetes mellitus. We report a rare case of a 58-year-old man who presented with portal hypertension and esophageal varices. The patient underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy for suspected pancreatic malignancy. However, a surgical pathology report retrieved during revision confirmed IgG4-associated autoimmune pancreatitis and documented diffuse sclerosing lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with dense periductal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, obliterative phlebitis, fibrosis/sclerosis, and increased IgG4-positive plasma cells (up to >50 per high-power field). Serum IgG4 was recorded as 5,521 mg/dL. Postoperatively, the patient developed insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, precluding corticosteroid therapy. Rituximab was initiated and the dosing interval was subsequently shortened after PET findings were interpreted as possible systemic involvement. Following treatment, recorded serum IgG4 values progressively decreased to 17 mg/dL. Follow-up endoscopy in 2023, supported by paired endoscopic images, demonstrated no visible esophageal varices in the imaged segment. This case describes an unusual and clinically relevant temporal association. However, the available data do not establish resolution of portal hypertension or a causal relationship between rituximab and the endoscopic finding.

items.title: Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease of the Temporomandibular Joint Extending into the External Auditory Canal and the Middle Ear, Coexisting with Otosclerosis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (CPPD) is caused by CPP crystals and rarely forms tumors in joints. The authors describe a case of tumoral CPPD in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), extending into the external auditory canal (EAC) and the middle ear. A 71-year-old man was referred to the department with a tentative diagnosis of CPPD in the right TMJ. Computed tomography showed the mass extending into the EAC, tympanic cavity, and bony Eustachian tube, with opacification of the mastoid cells. The audiogram revealed bilateral mixed hearing loss, suggesting the coexistence of bilateral otosclerosis. Partial resection of the mass and simultaneous implantation of a Baha® on the same side were performed. Histopathological findings revealed indistinct crystals in the surgical specimens. Calcium pyrophosphate crystals were identified using thin-film X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. The comorbidity of CPPD and otosclerosis in the same ear is a rare condition. Considering the unpredictable nature of CPPD, the authors opted for partial resection of the lesion involving the EAC and the middle ear to avoid any complications. Due to coexisting otosclerosis, Baha® played an important role in the auditory management of bilateral mixed hearing loss in this patient.

items.title: Effectiveness of Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Calcinosis of Dermatomyositis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis is an autoimmune connective tissue disease, in which calcinosis represents a late and often disabling complication, particularly in the juvenile form. The therapeutic management of calcinosis includes medical, surgical, and physiotherapy approaches, but no standardized treatment has been established. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) has emerged as a potential therapeutic alternative; however, reports of ESWT use in calcinosis associated with dermatomyositis remain rare. We report a case of dermatomyositis-associated calcinosis treated with ESWT, with favorable clinical outcomes, suggesting a potential therapeutic role for this approach in this challenging condition.

items.title: Granulomatous Interstitial Nephritis Associated With Adalimumab Therapy in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: We report the case of a 67-year-old female who presented with a history of asymptomatic rising of serum creatinine after receiving adalimumab therapy for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). A renal biopsy revealed granulomatous interstitial nephritis (GIN). After other causes of acute kidney injury were excluded, adalimumab was held, and steroid therapy was initiated. His kidney function improved. Based on this case report, adalimumab could be a rare cause of impaired kidney function and should not be considered a completely safe treatment or disregarded as a potential cause of renal complications, such as GIN, as diagnosed in our case.

items.title: Systemic Sclerosis Presenting With Long-Standing Peripheral Neuropathy and Delayed Multisystem Manifestations: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune connective tissue disorder characterized by immune dysregulation, microvascular injury, and progressive fibrosis involving the skin and internal organs. Although Raynaud phenomenon and cutaneous sclerosis are the hallmark manifestations, atypical presentations may significantly delay diagnosis. Peripheral neuropathy is an uncommon neurological manifestation and rarely precedes the diagnosis of SSc by several years. We report the case of a 62-year-old female who presented with a 20-year history of progressive distal paresthesia involving both upper and lower limbs, followed by recurrent lower limb ulceration and progressive unilateral lower-limb swelling associated with skin thickening and deformity. Nearly two decades after the onset of neurological symptoms, she developed progressive dysphagia, constitutional symptoms, exertional dyspnea, and pigmentary skin changes. Evaluation demonstrated positive antinuclear antibodies with strong anti-Ro52 and anti-RNP/Sm antibodies, mixed sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, pulmonary arterial hypertension, interstitial lung disease, moderate pericardial effusion, gastric antral vascular ectasia, and histopathological evidence of dermal sclerosis. She was diagnosed with SSc with overlap autoimmune features and managed through a multidisciplinary approach involving rheumatology, pulmonology, gastroenterology, rehabilitation medicine, and physiotherapy. This case illustrates an unusual neuropathy-predominant presentation in which peripheral nerve involvement preceded classical systemic manifestations by almost two decades. It highlights the importance of considering connective tissue diseases in patients presenting with chronic unexplained peripheral neuropathy, recurrent trophic ulceration, or progressive localized skin sclerosis. Early recognition of such atypical presentations may facilitate timely diagnosis, comprehensive organ screening, and administration of disease-modifying therapy before irreversible organ damage develops.

items.title: [Exploring comorbidity mechanism of systemic lupus erythematosus with osteoporosis and progress in TCM intervention from perspective of kidney-bone-immune axis].
items.abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus( SLE) have a significantly elevated risk of developing osteoporosis, a condition driven by complex interactions among immune inflammation, hormonal imbalances, and medication-related factors. Current western therapies often struggle to concurrently address immune regulation and bone protection. Based on the theory that " the kidney governs the bones and generates marrow", TCM characterizes the core pathogenesis as " kidney deficiency and marrow emptiness as the root, with heat toxin and blood stasis obstruction as the manifestations ". This concept aligns closely with the modern osteoimmunological concept of " immune-skeletal system crosstalk", giving rise to the integrated Chinese-western medicine theoretical framework known as the kidney-bone-immune axis. This review systematically summarized contemporary pathological mechanisms and TCM understanding of the pathogenesis of osteoporosis in SLE patients. It elaborated on the scientific implications of the kidney-boneimmune axis and highlighted the application of herbal formulas within the TCM syndrome differentiation system, as well as the osteoimmune-regulatory mechanisms of single and compound TCM herbs. Currently, research in this field remains nascent, lacking high-quality evidence and systematic mechanistic exploration. Future efforts should deepen the disease-pattern combination research paradigm and establish a multi-level evidence system to promote the systematic integration and clinical translation of TCM in the prevention and management of osteoporosis in SLE patients.

items.title: The EULAR points to consider regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in adult-onset Still's disease.
items.abstract: This study aims to formulate European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) points to consider (PtCs) regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD). The Task Force consisted of 23 members from 7 different European countries. A systematic literature review and a 3-round Delphi exercise involving European Experts were conducted to support the formulation of overarching principles and PtCs. Based on retrieved evidence and Experts' opinions, results of Delphi Rounds, and discussions, 3 overarching principles and 11 PtCs were developed. The Task Force agreed on the importance of an appropriate definition for the disease activity in AOSD to be valid, reliable, and easily transferable in a clinical setting. The development of specific criteria for the assessment of disease activity should include a precise definition of the clinical features that could better describe the patient condition. A clear definition of disease activity would help clinicians to adjust therapy and to identify refractory patients. A validated assessment of the disease activity is important to establish specifically designed and powered studies for comprehensive management of patients with AOSD. A uniform and reproducible definition of remission may facilitate the inclusion of a new therapeutic target into daily practice and clinical trials. The EULAR PtCs were produced regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in AOSD, to provide the basis for a clinical tool to be readily, reliably, and easily applied in clinical settings in order to improve patient management.

items.title: Effects of Exogenous Relaxin on Dry Eye in an Experimental Sjögren's disease (SS) Mouse Model.
items.abstract: To evaluate the potential of exogenous relaxin (RLX) as a treatment for dry eye disease (DED) in an experimental animal model of Sjögren's disease (SS). Nonobese diabetic female (NOD) mice with SS-associated DED received RLX-based or vehicle eye drops (100ng/mL) four times daily for 30 days. Clinical evaluations included measurements of tear production, assessment of keratitis, and histological analysis of the exorbital lacrimal gland. Inflammatory cytokine expression was measured using PCR. RLX-treated mice showed significant improvement in tear production and keratitis reversal. Qualitative histological analysis suggested better preservation of lacrimal gland architecture, with more evident acinar and ductal structures in the RLX-treated group. PCR analysis demonstrated reduced inflammatory cytokine expression (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12a, IL-17a, TNFα, and IFNγ), and increased expression of RLX and its receptor RXFP1 in the RLX-treated group CONCLUSIONS: Exogenous relaxin shows therapeutic potential for DED in SS, demonstrated by clinical improvements and reduced inflammatory markers in an animal model of SS.

items.title: The role of immune aging in rheumatoid arthritis and its clinical and therapeutic significance.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease, and its onset and progression are closely related to age-related remodeling of the immune system. Immunosenescence refers to age-related changes in the overall structure and function of the immune system; inflammaging is a persistent, low-grade, systemic inflammatory state; cellular senescence refers to a relatively stable cell cycle arrest and functional remodeling of cells under continuous stress. These three are interrelated but correspond to the immune system, systemic inflammatory environment, and cellular state, respectively; therefore, they should not be used interchangeably. In RA, especially elderly-onset RA (EORA), immune age-related changes may occur earlier or be more severe. Human studies on RA mainly support that immune cell lineage remodeling, senescence-associated cell phenotypes, and changes in inflammatory mediators are associated with disease activity, structural damage, and some extra-articular comorbidities. Immunosenescence may compromise T-cell, B-cell, and innate immune functions; concurrently, local cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) may drive synovial and bone marrow microenvironment remodeling, while inflammaging may further amplify systemic inflammation. Impaired immune clearance, accumulation of senescent cells, and SASP release may establish a self-perpetuating cycle and are associated with autoantibody production, bone loss, cartilage damage, and cardiovascular and neuropsychiatric comorbidities. However, causal evidence for SASP-driven RA synovitis and the efficacy of senolytic interventions is still primarily derived from experimental arthritis, osteoarthritis, and other non-RA disease models. This article clarifies the definitions and delineates the applicable boundaries of these three terms, reviews their systemic phenotypes, cell lineage characteristics, and molecular basis in RA, especially EORA, analyzes the links between immune age and disease activity, autoantibodies, synovial microenvironment, bone and cartilage damage, and extra-articular manifestations, and evaluates the potential benefits, risks, and evidence limitations of traditional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), biologic agents, and emerging senescence-targeting strategies. By constructing an integrated framework covering immune system remodeling, local cellular senescence, inflammatory amplification, and clinical outcomes, this article aims to provide a theoretical basis for further research on EORA risk stratification and immunosenescence-related interventions, rather than directly translating unverified mechanisms into clinical conclusions.

items.title: Copper single-atom carbon dots hydrogel resets oxidative and immune homeostasis for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis pathogenesis is perpetuated by a self-sustaining oxidative stress-immunodysregulation circuit. To address the limitations of conventional antioxidants, including unclear catalytic structures and single catalytic activity, we engineered copper single-atom carbon dots via topological transformation of sodium copper chlorophyllin. Encapsulated within a pH-responsive injectable hydrogel, this system achieves targeted delivery to inflamed joints, where it simultaneously scavenges superoxide anions and hydrogen peroxide, breaking the reactive oxygen species-inflammation cycle. Treatment reprograms macrophage polarization, suppresses pathogenic B-cell infiltration, and mitigates cartilage erosion. By integrating nature-inspired atomic catalysis with intelligent biomaterial engineering, this approach establishes a paradigm for resetting oxidative-immune microenvironments in autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Allergic profile and pre-diagnostic exposure to allergen-specific immunotherapy in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA): a single-centre retrospective observational study.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) combines asthma, eosinophilic inflammation and small- to medium-vessel vasculitis. The relationship between conventional allergic phenotypes, allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT) and subsequent EGPA remains uncertain. To describe specialist-adjudicated allergic manifestations in a selected EGPA cohort and explore whether pre-diagnostic AIT exposure was associated with age at EGPA onset or clinical phenotype. We retrospectively analysed 53 patients with expert-diagnosed EGPA, complete historical records and an allergy evaluation adequate to classify aeroallergen sensitisation, respiratory allergy, food allergy and drug hypersensitivity. Continuous variables were assessed for normality and compared using Mann-Whitney U tests; categorical variables were compared using Fisher exact tests. Analyses were exploratory. Twenty-five patients (47.2%) had at least one recorded allergic manifestation. Aeroallergen sensitisation was present in 14/53 (26.4%), food allergy in 4/53 (7.5%), drug hypersensitivity in 13/53 (24.5%) and another specialist-adjudicated allergic manifestation in 1/53 (1.9%); categories overlapped. Thirteen of 14 aeroallergen-sensitized patients had multiple sensitisations. Thirteen patients were considered eligible for AIT and 7 received AIT before EGPA diagnosis. The median interval from AIT initiation to EGPA diagnosis was 13.1 years (interquartile range 5.5-20.0). No AIT-related adverse reaction was documented in available records. Exploratory comparisons did not identify statistically significant differences between allergic and non-allergic patients or between AIT-treated and AIT-eligible untreated patients. In this selected single-centre cohort, allergic manifestations were frequent, but the inclusion process precludes population-level prevalence estimates. No association between pre-diagnostic AIT exposure and age at EGPA onset or exploratory phenotype measures was observed. No signals of potentially AIT-triggered cases were found. However, the very small AIT subgroup, retrospective design and non-systematic safety ascertainment do not exclude clinically relevant effects and do not establish causality or AIT safety. Key Points • Allergic manifestations, particularly aeroallergen sensitisation and drug hypersensitivity, were frequent in this selected single-centre EGPA cohort. • Allergic status was not associated with a clearly distinct EGPA phenotype, although subgroup comparisons were exploratory and limited by the small sample size. • No association was observed between previous allergen-specific immunotherapy and the age or clinical pattern of EGPA onset.

items.title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.

items.title: Double-negative B cells mediate the causal association between rheumatoid arthritis and interstitial lung disease: a two-step Mendelian randomization mediation study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) elevates interstitial lung disease (ILD) risk, yet the underlying mediating immune cells remain unknown. This study sought peripheral immune phenotypes driving the causal pathway from RA to ILD. A two-step Mendelian randomization (MR) mediation analysis was performed using European GWAS data: RA (14,361 cases/43,923), 731 immune cell traits, and ILD from FinnGen R13 (6,733 cases/493,453). Step 1 applied inverse variance weighted (IVW) MR to estimate RA effects on immune cells; Step 2 tested immune cell effects on ILD. Mediation was validated via joint significance and parametric bootstrapping (10,000 resamples) with BCa 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RA exerted a causal risk-increasing effect on ILD (β = 0.166, P = 4.26 × 10⁻⁸). Fifty-three immune traits showed nominal significance in Step 1, 15 passing FDR correction. CD19⁺IgD⁻CD27⁻ DN B cells reached nominal significance (P = 0.028) but not FDR significance (q = 0.512) in Step 1, yet were the only trait significantly associated with ILD in Step 2 (β₂ = 0.060, P = 0.027). Bootstrapping verified a small but significant indirect effect (β = 0.0039, 95% BCa CI 0.0009-0.0153, P = 0.050; mediation proportion = 2.3%), consistent across sensitivity tests. DN B cells partially mediate the causal RA-ILD relationship. Our genetic evidence highlights B cell dysfunction as a mechanistic link and identifies DN B cells as candidate biomarkers for RA-related interstitial lung complications. Key Points • Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with elevated interstitial lung disease (ILD) risk, yet the underlying causal pathway remains poorly defined. • A two-step Mendelian randomization mediation design was applied to identify double-negative (DN) B cells (CD19⁺IgD⁻CD27⁻) as a potential mediator linking RA to ILD. • Genetically predisposed RA was causally associated with increased DN B cell proportions, which in turn were associated with higher ILD risk. • These findings indicate DN B cells may serve as a potential immunological link between RA and ILD, meriting further investigation as a candidate direction for early intervention research.

items.title: Deguelin Alleviates Renal Tubular Epithelial Cell Injury in Lupus Nephritis by Inhibiting the PI3K/Akt Signaling Pathway.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is one of the most serious complications of systemic lupus erythematosus. Circadian rhythm disorders are related to the pathogenesis of LN. This study aims to identify the core circadian rhythm-related genes in LN and identify the potential natural active compounds for LN treatment. In the present study, cyclin A2 (CCNA2) and cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 3 (CDKN3) were identified as the core targets most related to the circadian rhythm of LN. Both of them were upregulated in blood and kidney tissue samples in LN and had high diagnostic efficacy. Deguelin had strong binding capabilities with CCNA2 and CDKN3 proteins. Deguelin could dose-dependently alleviate lipopolysaccharide-induced human kidney-2 (HK-2) cell damage, inhibit cell apoptosis and the release of inflammatory factors, downregulate the mRNA and protein expression levels of core genes CCNA2 and CDKN3, and inhibit the activation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt signaling pathway. The protective effect of deguelin could be reversed by AKT activator SC79 treatment. In summary, CCNA2 and CDKN3 are core genes related to the circadian rhythm in LN. Deguelin probably alleviates renal tubular epithelial cell injury by modulating the expression levels of core genes CCNA2 and CDKN3, inhibiting the activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, and thus has the potential to become a therapeutic agent for LN.

items.title: Assessing the quality of end-of-life care in systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune disease with the highest mortality among rheumatic diseases, yet little is known about the quality of end-of-life care in SSc. To evaluate end-of-life care in SSc against the Australian National Consensus Statement's Essential Elements for high-quality end-of-life care and compare care between palliative care unit (PCU) and non-PCU deaths. This retrospective single-centre study included adults with SSc who died between 2013 and 2023 at a tertiary SSc referral centre. Terminal admission records for expected deaths were mapped to the National Consensus domains. Fisher exact and Mann-Whitney U tests compared PCU and non-PCU deaths. Thirty-three patients died. Six unexpected deaths were excluded, leaving 15 PCU and 12 non-PCU deaths. Multidisciplinary involvement was extensive, particularly from rheumatology and allied health. Palliative care engagement was common, goals of care were frequently reviewed and communication about dying with next-of-kin occurred in most cases. Patients dying outside the PCU had lower rates of documented recognition of dying, significantly greater intensive care involvement and more frequent medical emergency team calls. They also received more potentially non-beneficial investigations and treatments during the final 48 h of life and incurred substantially higher terminal admission costs. End-of-life care in SSc was broadly consistent with the National Consensus standards, identifying strong rheumatology involvement, multidisciplinary care and frequent palliative care referral. However, differences in care according to site of death highlight opportunities to increase proactive palliative care involvement and regular review of goals of care to ensure high-quality end-of-life care across all settings.

items.title: Evolution of outcome assessment in clinical trials of rheumatoid arthritis: A scoping review.
items.abstract: To identify, map, and synthesize the outcomes reported in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and describe how these outcomes have changed over time throughout the 20th and 21st centuries. A scoping review was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Electronic searches were performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, PEDro, and Google Scholar from January 1989 to May 2026. Randomized clinical trials involving adults with rheumatoid arthritis were eligible. Five independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Reported outcomes were classified into conceptual domains and analyzed chronologically to identify temporal trends in outcome assessment. The search identified 5209 records, of which 611 randomized clinical trials met the eligibility criteria. Disease activity outcomes remained the most consistently reported across all decades, evolving from individual clinical measures toward standardized composite indices, including ACR response criteria, DAS, DAS28, SDAI, and CDAI. Outcome assessment progressively expanded to incorporate structural damage, patient-reported outcomes, physical function, health-related quality of life, imaging, laboratory biomarkers, safety, and health-economic measures. Recent trials increasingly emphasized remission, treat-to-target strategies, advanced imaging techniques, validated patient-reported outcome measures, and biomarker-based assessments, reflecting a more comprehensive and patient-centered approach to rheumatoid arthritis management. Outcome assessment in rheumatoid arthritis clinical trials has evolved substantially over the past four decades, transitioning from symptom-focused evaluation to multidimensional assessment encompassing clinical, structural, functional, biological, and patient-centered domains. This review synthesizes evidence from 611 randomized clinical trials and provides a comprehensive mapping of the historical evolution of outcome measurement, offering a valuable reference for future clinical research and the development of standardized core outcome sets.

items.title: Patient perspectives on simultaneous methotrexate-folic acid intake to improve adherence in rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: To assess real-world adherence to folic acid (FA) supplementation with methotrexate (MTX) and patient perceptions of a simplified, same-day dosing strategy in RA. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey co-designed with patient representatives and distributed by the French patient association AFPric. RA patients treated with MTX were eligible. The questionnaire captured MTX and FA regimens, omissions, adverse events and attitudes toward same-day MTX and FA administration. Analyses were descriptive with prespecified subgroup comparisons. Among 967 respondents (86.8% women; mean age 62.4 years), 86.7% reported once-weekly FA supplementation. Overall, 25.5% reported at least occasional FA omission, with omissions more frequent among long-term MTX users. Nausea after MTX was reported by 46.6% of respondents and by 52.6% of those reporting FA omissions. A same-day MTX and FA regimen was perceived as simpler by 30.5% and 41.5% believed it could reduce FA omission. Overall, 64.8% indicated that they would be willing to participate in a randomised controlled trial evaluating simultaneous administration. One in four people with RA treated with MTX reported FA omissions. Many respondents believed that a same-day regimen could reduce FA omissions, and interest in participating in a clinical trial was high. These findings support the feasibility of prospectively evaluating whether same-day MTX and FA administration may improve adherence and tolerability in selected patients, particularly those receiving once-weekly FA supplementation, without compromising MTX effectiveness.

items.title: A 12-week randomized controlled trial of the dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH) diet in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis: Effects on disease activity and outcomes.
items.abstract: Dietary interventions may improve rheumatoid arthritis (RA) outcomes through anti-inflammatory and metabolic pathways. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on disease activity and treatment outcomes in patients with seropositive RA. In this 12-week parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 82 patients with seropositive RA were randomly assigned to a DASH diet intervention (n = 40) or a control group maintaining their usual diet (n = 42). The primary outcome was change in disease activity assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS-28 E SR). Secondary outcomes included change in DAS-28 based on C-reactive protein (DAS-28 CRP), as well as tender and swollen joint counts, ESR, CRP, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for pain and general health, the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), and the Short Form-36 (SF-36). Adherence to the intervention was evaluated using the DASH diet score. Assessments were performed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Data were analyzed according to the intention-to-treat principle. Repeated clinical outcomes were analyzed using robust mixed ANOVA or generalized estimating equations (GEE), as appropriate. Of the 82 randomized patients, 49 completed the 12-week study. Adherence to the DASH diet increased significantly in the intervention group compared with the control group (p < 0.001). From baseline to Week 12, DAS-28 ESR decreased by 0.92 points in the DASH group versus 0.17 points in the control group, corresponding to a 0.75-point greater reduction (group × time interaction, p = 0.001). Significant between-group differences in change were also observed for DAS-28 CRP (-0.62), ESR (-3.90 mm/h), VAS-pain (-2.19), VAS-general health (-2.12), and HAQ (-0.38) (all group × time p˂0.05). For SF-36, significant between-group differences in change were observed for physical functioning (+10.15), role-physical (+47.30), bodily pain (+22.17), vitality (+18.52), role-emotional (+38.61), and mental health (+12.06) (all group × time p < 0.05). CRP, tender and swollen joint counts did not show significant group × time interactions (p > 0.05). Furthermore, in the intervention group, improvements in DASH diet adherence were negatively correlated with changes in DAS-28 ESR and DAS-28 CRP scores (both p < 0.05). A 12-week DASH dietary intervention may provide clinically meaningful improvements in disease activity and patient-reported outcomes in patients with seropositive RA. These findings support the potential role of the DASH dietary pattern as a promising dietary approach to complement the management of RA. However, the relatively high attrition rate should be considered when interpreting the findings. This trial is registered with Clinicaltrials.gov (ID: NCT07170033). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07170033.

items.title: Identification of the Proapoptotic Mechanism of Astragalosides in Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy Based on HPLC, Bioinformatics and Network Pharmacology.
items.abstract: Astragalosides (ASTs), principal active saponins derived from Astragalus, exert prominent therapeutic efficacy against Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). However, few studies have investigated the molecular mechanism of ASTs in RA therapy. AST components were qualitatively and quantitatively analyzed by HPLC. RA-related Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) were acquired from the GSE77298 dataset, and AST target genes were predicted via multiple databases. Core hub genes and signaling pathways were screened through bioinformatics analyses, including GO/KEGG enrichment, PPI network and MCODE modularity analysis. Molecular docking was performed to evaluate the binding affinity between ASTs and core apoptotic genes. Cell phenotypic assays, qRT-PCR, Western blot and CASP8 siRNA interference experiments were conducted to validate the regulatory effect of ASTs on the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 axis in MH7A cells. In total, 5781 DEGs were obtained from the GSE77298 dataset, 496 ASTs-related genes were predicted, among which 156 intersected. They were enriched in 3345 significant GO terms and 121 significant KEGG pathways. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses validated that ATM, CASP8, and XIAP mediate AST-induced MH7A cell apoptosis via the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 axis. ASTs decrease cellular proliferation and induce apoptosis in MH7A cells. Moreover, ASTs reduced the expression of XIAP and increased the expression of ATM and CASP8 at both the mRNA and protein levels. In addition, ASTs reversed the effects of siRNA-mediated CASP8 silencing on the mRNA expression of CASP3, ATM, and XIAP. ASTs can promote apoptosis in MH7A cells, and the underlying mechanism may involve regulation of the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 signaling axis.
